title: Eigentlich super, aber...
body:
Ich habe alle (!) ToDo-Apps probiert und TickTick spielt eigentlich ganz vorne mit - wenn da nicht immer noch das eine große Manko wäre: der Kalender bzw. dessen Integration. Nur auf sehr umständlichem Weg ist es möglich Kalender-Termine anzulegen, das macht den ganzen Workflow kaputt. Und da die Synchronisation mit dem Google-Kalender auch noch bis zu 12 Stunden dauert, ist die App leider unbenutzbar. Wenn Termine gleich anlegbar/editierbar sind wie Tasks (in der Listen- und v.a. Kalender-Ansicht), dann vergebe ich gerne 7 Sterne. 😉

Update: alle paar Monate gebe ich TickTick eine Chance (um zu sehen, ob sich was am obigen Thema geändert hat) und habe auch diesmal wieder ein Monatsabo abgeschlossen. Leider aber ist alles noch genau gleich. Ein paar tolle Funktionen sind zwar dazugekommen, aber das Kalender-Problem ist für mich immer noch das Killer-Kriterium.

title: Discover an amazing app designed to help you stay on top of your game with effortless reminders, eff
body:
The application has highly beneficial features designed to enhance productivity and organisation. Among its many tools are comprehensive habit trackers that allow users to monitor their daily routines and progress over time. The app also includes robust to-do lists that help users prioritise tasks efficiently and customizable reminders that can be categorised for better organisation.

In addition, an intuitive countdown feature enables users to track the days remaining until a specific event or to keep a record of how many days have passed since a notable date, which can be particularly useful for project deadlines or personal milestones. Furthermore, the app incorporates an Eisenhower Matrix, a strategic tool that helps users distinguish between urgent and essential tasks, facilitating more effective decision-making and time management.

This is hands down the best app I’ve ever had for organising both your calendar and your to do list. FINALLY! Someone finally realised calendar and to do lists need to go together, and the app is free with an optional upgrade. 

Also this is one of the most user friendly apps I’ve come across and I don’t dish out the compliments lightly. It’s very intuitive and the developers appear to have thought of everything. You have your calendar with multiple views, your to do lists where you can organise into multiple categories, an event countdown and even a pros and cons section to help you figure out priorities and importance. 

 I have ADHD and this app is my daily go to so I keep up with everything and anything, it’s a blessing, thank you 🙏

My bank account is empty so I checked my transaction history, and this app charged me a fortune for a yearly subscription. I’m not even using it!!!!! I need a habit tracking app BECAUSE I have a terrible memory for things like cancelling subscriptions within the free trial period. Automatic subscriptions after a free trial are predatory and you (the developers) know what you’re doing by coercing people into it. I’m happy to sign up (and pay) for an app that works for me, but this one doesn’t.

title: Highly recommend this app!
body:

Mainly what I am loving about TickTick is you create a list of tasks and it will push those tasks by date to the in- app calendar. So I’ve made a list of the upcoming school holidays, and a separate list of my assessment due dates, and all those dates have been pushed to the calendar. The task list counts down how many days until X in date order, while the calendar gives me a macro view of the month. Giving me two views of these things helps my brain to prioritise and plan. 

This app is excellent and quite reasonably priced for such a developed product. My only feedback request would be for a ‘Today’ button  whilst in calendar view that instantly scrolls back to today, saving on having to do it manually. Please do this!

My favourite features:

- when you tick items off in your calendar they still display, but greyed out so you know what’s completed.
- both the month view mode to overview and plan tasks over weeks ahead, but also the week view mode to arrange tasks in more specific hour/minute order for busier days 
- recurring tasks have a lot of customisation available 
- could share lists and calendars with colleagues for shared projects

title: Best task and note app
body:
Tick Tick is by far the best task and note app I have used.

I used to use Wunderlist before it became extinct. I tried a few apps and found that Tick Tick was clearly the best, even better than Wunderlist.

I use Tick Tick for the personal tasks I need to complete and more so for note taking. 

I love that there is enough hierarchy to organise my lists without being over complicated.

Being able to switch a list between a checklist and notes layout is really handy. And when I want a bulleted list, the shortcut of typing a dash before text makes it so easy on the app.

Tags for another layer of grouping really helps to highlight tasks from different lists.

Reminders can be useful too.

The fact that it has a desktop app is awesome for when I’m in front of my work or home computer and makes it easy when there is a lot of typing or copying and pasting to do which can be frustrating on a phone.

For work I use ClickUp which is amazing and flexible but overkill for personal use and needs to be used on a computer as there is too many features which makes it clunky for a device app.

Tick Tick does everything I need.

title: App is fine, but support is slow and often dismissive or not helpful
body:
I’ve used TickTick for years, and was fairly happy with it overall, and have been a paid user for years, but I’m moving away from it for two main reasons: Generally unimpressive support, and an instance of data loss that they seem disinterested in helping with.

My advice to those thinking of using TickTick is: The app is generally good, but support and the only available support mechanism is slow and painful. If you ever need to use it you will not likely come away happy.

I’ve used the support for the app a number of times over several years, mostly for suggestions/questions, and have never been impressed with it. The support mechanism seems to be limited to a chat style system within the app itself and, in my experience, you can go days (sometimes even weeks/months) before you get a response. How is something supposed to be resolved in a timely fashion if the chat turnaround is measured in days rather than hours or minutes?

With regards to my data loss situation, I had a list with 5-6 sections and more than 80 items arranged across them. One day I opened the list to find that suddenly all items had somehow been moved into a single section. I’m now 15 days into trying to get this resolved and the (minimal) replies I’ve had from the company have largely ignored my questions or requests for information, and the one fix they did (maybe, I’m not sure what they actually did, because no details) didn’t fix anything, as far as I can tell. They said to contact them if that didn’t fix things, so I did, immediately, and it’s now been 5 days and I haven’t heard a thing. Not from the chat system, and not from their twitter account, which is either unobservant (they’ve replied to me in the past), or just ignoring me.

title: My favourite task manager, by far
body:

Importance indicators, being able to indicate progress on a task, having lists auto sort tasks into different time frames - this app has so many features I don't know how I lived without. Every other app I've had some frustration or problem with, but never TickTick. 5 stars (and I'm not even on the premium version!).

title: Segredo
body:
O que muitos buscam segredo para o sucesso encontra na funcionalidade que este app oferece, organizar, planejar e lembrar suas tarefas. Com consistência o tempo fará o efeito composto pra você atingir seus objetivos

Sobre as funcionalidades estão bem dispostas com ícones intuitivos, sendo possível colocar data e horário para realizar a tarefa e até mesmo tempo para enviar notificação antes (30min, 1h) para te lembrar o que você planejou. 
Fora as listas sendo possível planejar e organizar áreas da vida diferentes, ou até mesmo prioridades de tarefas diferentes (tudo depende de como você vai usar as listas e tags e filtros. Sou usuário do plano gratuito, e com isso você já tem tudo que precisa.

title: Incrível! Porém…
body:
The organization and layout are amazing. I’ve tested many others, but this one is the best. To make it perfect, it needs improvements in two areas: using AI to create scheduled tasks via voice command, and syncing across the Apple ecosystem. Currently, it doesn’t update automatically—if something changes on one device, you need to open the app on the other for it to sync. This makes using the widgets (which are one of the most perfect features of this app) a bit impractical.

Muito incrível a organização e layout. Já testei muitos outros, mas esse é o melhor. Pra ficar perfeito, precisa melhorar: Uso de IA para criar tarefas agendadas por comando de voz e a atualização entre o eco sistema apple, pois não atualiza sozinho, se mudar algo em um dispositivo, precisa abrir o app no outro para atualizar. Isso torna pouco pratico o uso dos Widgets(que são uma das coisas mais perfeitas desse app)

title: Quase excelente
body:
Já tentei muitos apps. Dois melhores: TickTick e Todoist. TickTick ganha pela capacidade de marcar o tempo investido em cada tarefa, o que serve pra calcular horas de trabalho para apresentar a clientes, estimar tempos mais precisamente no futuro, e muitas outros insights. Ganha também no registro e acompanhamento de hábitos (que diz que tem mas na verdade não tem no Todoist). Ganha pela integração com iCal, coisa simples que o Todoist se recusa a entregar. Perde feio no uso de linguagem natural para criar agendamentos, que no Todoist é super eficaz enquanto no TickTick é truncado e atrapalhado. 
No geral, ambos são ótimos, mas fico com TickTick.

title: Se você já tentou tudo…
body:
Se você já tentou tudo para organizar sua vida e acabou soterrado por aplicativos complexos ou listas de papel perdidas, o TickTick é o ponto final da sua busca.
O que torna este app tão especial é o equilíbrio perfeito entre simplicidade e robustez. Ele não é apenas um gerenciador de tarefas; é uma central de produtividade completa.

Diferente de outros players do mercado, o TickTick parece entender como o cérebro humano funciona: ele remove o atrito e deixa o caminho livre para o que realmente importa: fazer as coisas acontecerem. É, sem dúvida, a ferramenta definitiva para quem quer transformar o caos em clareza.

title: Adicionem bloco de tempo no calendário e gráficos melhores pros hábitos
body:
O TickTick é excelente e muito eficiente no dia a dia. Porém, seria incrível ter blocos de tempo mais estruturais no calendário (não apenas tarefas com horário), permitindo organizar o dia por áreas como Trabalho, Saúde, Estudos etc., com a possibilidade de adicionar tarefas dentro desses blocos.

Também seria ótimo melhorar os gráficos de hábitos, com análises mais profundas e visuais mais modernos, mostrando evolução por área da vida e não apenas streaks simples. Isso deixaria o app ainda mais completo e estratégico.

title: Life-changing
body:
Atualmente eu simplesmente não consigo mais viver sem o app. Eu tenho TDAH e sempre tive um pensamento bem acelerado e me sentia meio desesperado por não conseguir anotar e organizar essas ideias/pensamentos direito. O TickTick veio pra realmente mudar minha realidade e eu realmente não me importo de pagar o plano pago do app. Realmente vale a pena. O app tem TUDO que um app que se preze tem que ter e ainda um pouco mais. Parabéns aos desenvolvedores.

Se eu fosse sugerir uma coisa seria a inserção de IA pra auxiliar a melhorar a escrita das tarefas e facilitar o usuário a criar tarefas atingíveis. O “Todoist” tem esse recurso e eu gostava muito.

title: Fantastic
body:
It's awesome to use this app. The integration with the Eisenhower matrix, Pomodoro technique, and habit tracker provides tools that make it an excellent product among productivity apps.  

If I may offer a suggestion: I think it would be fantastic if TickTick used LLM integration to understand natural voice-to-text commands. This could create multiple tasks at once, reschedule delayed tasks (which would be especially helpful for users with ADHD), and intelligently fit daily tasks into available hours.

title: Não sei como vivi tanto tempo sem esse app incrível!
body: Encontrei o tick tick há 2 semanas procurando por uma agenda aqui na App Store. Sempre tentei me adaptar a planners físicos, acho que por uma moda do consumo exagerado, mas nunca consegui, por ser algo extremamente chato e nada funcional. Precisar abrir uma agenda todo dia, andar com ela pra cima e pra baixo… essas coisas dificultavam muito minha adesão. Mas com o tick tick foi muito diferente. Tudo no app é simples e prático. Consigo adicionar minhas tarefas do dia a dia e meus compromissos com muita facilidade e visualizar minha semana de maneira bastante clara. Dá pra perceber que o app foi feito por pessoas que realmente já usaram diversas ferramentas de planejamento e tentaram incluir tudo num único app. Desde as listas, os hábitos, a matriz de eisenhower… tudo é incrível e muito útil. Minha única ressalva ate o momento (posso voltar pra atualizar depois com novas considerações) é que as funcionalidades no Apple Watch são limitadas. Queria ter mais opções de visualização por lá. Tipo um widget para hábitos, ou para consumo de água. Se tivesse coisas desse tipo conseguiria descartar mais 2 apps meus!

title: Integrar hábitos com Apple healt
body:

1- completar hábitos automaticamente e registrar quando você passa da meta

title: Bugs e Problemas Recorrentes
body:
Paguei pela assinatura e tive algumas decepções.

1. O app possui muitos bugs, especialmente na parte da sincronização.
2. As vezes, enquanto eu registrava atividades, eu mudava a tela e acabava que os registros sumiam. Isso ocorreu muito enquanto usava o calendário 
3. A assinatura não é barata (em termos de Real brasileiro o plano anual custa 1/11 do salário mínimo)

Algumas sugestões de Melhoria:

- O TickTick devia ter algo como uma Escola de Aprendizado, como existe pro Todoist e pro Miro. Assim, os usuários não precisariam se basear apenas em YouTube.
- Correção dos Bugs
- Redução no custo do plano
- Widgets interativos para a nova versão

Se minha esposa compartilha um evento do Google Agenda dela comigo, eu não consigo aceitar ou rejeitar no app. Pior ainda é eu não conseguir criar um evento para convidar alguém. Então para quem não compartilha tarefas e eventos com outras pessoas que tem outras agendas, este app é maravilhoso mesmo. Para quem compartilha, tem essa falta grave. title: O Melhor aplicativo de produtividade !
body:
O TickTick é a melhor e mais completa ferramenta do mercado hoje. Une todos os itens essenciais para uma boa produtividade: Tarefas, Calendário, Notas, Hábitos e pomodoro. Uso há 03 anos e indico de olhos fechados. Aqui vai alguns pontos que seria interessante que os desenvolvedores implementassem para agregar ainda mais o aplicativo e deixa-lo mais completo ainda:

1. Uma tela inicial, estilo Dashboard. Onde fosse possível ter uma “visão geral” de tudo ( notas, lembretes, tarefas e eventos) de uma forma bonita e minimalista- exemplo: Tela inicial do Evernote

2. Agregar mais nas ferramentas de notas, com mais itens para agregar no texto: cores diferentes de palavras, ferramentas de estilo de palavras e etc- exemplo: Ferramentas de notas do Notion

3. Opção de colocar horário nos hábitos dos calendários. Em vez deles aparecerem na parte superior, fosse possível eles aparecerem no horário destinado. Exemplo: Exercícios fisicos todos os dias às 16h

4. Incluir Mapas mentais seria um extremo diferencial. Hoje a única plataforma do mercado que possui mapa mental é o Clickup

5- Uma aba de tarefas especial para Metas e objetivos, onde tivesse uma “aparência” diferente e que estimulasse a ideia de objetivos

title: Bom mas tem pontos importantes de melhoria
body:
É muito bom pra organização e uma das grandes vantagens pra mim é que tem versão pra qualquer dispositivo. Uso no celular, tablet e PC, e ainda em sistemas operacionais diferentes. Porém, apesar da experiência ser parecida e ter sincronia de tasks e hábitos em todos os dispositivos. 
As configurações/preferências e a inscrição dos calendários não são sincronizadas em todos os dispositivos. Ou seja, se você definiu suas preferências e inscreveu calendários no mobile, terá de fazer tudo denovo no PC. Pode ser um tanto frustrante ter esse trabalho várias vezes, mas depois do setup feito, as informações exibidas serão as mesmas.
Outro ponto é que você só faz inscrição nos calendários e não integração, ou seja, só vai visualizar o que já tem agendado, se precisar mudar algo vai ter que abrir os calendários de origem da mesma forma.

title: Almost perfect | quase perfeito
body:
I'm enjoying the paid version. The habits feature into a To-Do app is the best idea for a life-tracking app.
Pros: very very customizable alerts and recurrences. 
Cons: different calendars between platform versions (Windows app or Chrome extension doesn't have a 3day calendar, the iPhone app has more options than others)
 
I need within habits feature:
- Please make customizable habits equal your alerts settings. Some habits don't run every day
- ...and a 'skip' feature is useful sometimes.
 
Idea: Eisenhower's box. The TickTick app already has priorities and dates, with some adjustments I think this view is possible and useful ;D
 
With it, I give 5 stars easily.
 
 
---- Portuguese ----
Eu estou gostando da versão paga. O recurso de hábitos em um aplicativo de tarefas é a melhor ideia para um aplicativo de rastreamento de vida.
 
Prós: alertas muito personalizáveis e recorrências.
 
Contras: calendários diferentes entre as versões de plataforma (a versão do Windows ou a extensão do Chrome não tem um calendário de três dias, o aplicativo do iPhone tem mais opções do que outras)
 
** Eu adoraria que o recurso de hábitos tivesse:
- Por favor, faça hábitos personalizáveis igual a configuração dos alertas. Alguns hábitos não correm todos os dias
- ... e um recurso de "pular" é útil às vezes.
 
Idéia: caixa de Eisenhower. O aplicativo TickTick já tem prioridades e datas, com alguns ajustes acho que essa visão é possível e útil; D
 
Com isso, eu dou 5 estrelas facilmente.

title: Une excellente application multiplateforme avec IA native et intégration ChatGPT !
body:
Après plusieurs années avec Things 3, j’ai décidé de passer à TickTick et je suis vraiment impressionné !

J’utilise un gestionnaire de tâches autant dans ma vie personnelle que professionnelle. L’un des principaux facteurs qui m’ont poussé à quitter Things 3 était son fonctionnement limité à l’écosystème Apple, alors que mon environnement professionnel repose principalement sur Windows.

TickTick me permet enfin de gérer mes tâches de façon transparente entre mon iPhone, mon iPad et mes ordinateurs Windows, sans compromis sur les fonctionnalités.

Mais ce qui fait réellement la différence pour moi, c’est l’intégration avec ChatGPT. Je peux créer et organiser mes tâches, ajouter des échéances et gérer mes listes directement depuis une conversation. C’est un gain de temps considérable, particulièrement dans mon utilisation hybride combinant un notebook papier pour mes notes et TickTick pour le suivi de mes actions.

J’apprécie également la richesse des fonctionnalités, la flexibilité de l’application et la possibilité de l’adapter à ma façon de travailler, plutôt que l’inverse.

Après toutes ces années avec Things 3, je ne regrette absolument pas ma transition. Une excellente découverte que je recommande sans hésitation !

title: Keeps me on track
body:
I’m a senior executive assistant and over that past 3 1/2 years I’ve supported multiple c-suite leaders at my company.  At times 5 of them at once.  I love my job but it gets crazy with so many variables.  I tried many different apps and Tick Tick was the one I kept coming back to.  There are certain things I found worked for me through experience, and this app allowed me to customize my lists and tasks as needed. 
I have a separate notebook for each exec that is sectioned off by weekly meetings, to dos and notes for the exec such as travel info. I then created a To Do list with filters that will display the tasks I list within each execs folder. 
We also use Slack and having the option to add something from Slack to Tick Tick is really nice.  
I do find for my needs having the premium version is a must but for everything it helps me do it’s worth every penny (which is not much at all!).

title: The Best Productivity App Out There – A Lifesaver for ADHD & Busy Lives!
body:
I’ve been using TickTick daily for the past few years, and I can honestly say it has completely transformed how I manage my routine. As a premium user, it’s one of the best investments I’ve made — incredibly affordable for the value it brings. However, the free version is also amazing with many functionalities.

I live a very busy life, juggling multiple roles and responsibilities, and like many people with ADHD, I often struggle to focus and keep track of everything on my own. TickTick has been my anchor. From breaking down big projects into small steps to organizing daily tasks, setting priorities, and syncing across all my devices — it keeps me on track effortlessly. I love the fact that there is a Google Extension and Desktop version too. It works seamlessly in both Windows and Macbooks.

One of my favorite features? Reminders and recurring tasks — they’ve even helped me stay consistent with taking my medications, which has made a real difference for my health. I also love the calendar view, Pomodoro timer, and the clean, user-friendly interface. It’s powerful yet intuitive.

TickTick doesn’t just help me get more done — it helps me feel more in control, less overwhelmed, and more capable every day.

If you’re looking for a tool to boost your productivity, especially if you deal with focus issues or simply have a packed schedule, TickTick is an absolute game changer. The best app out there for sure, and I have tried and used many apps already. Look no further, TickTick is your best ally.

title: Best app ever!
body:
I use it as my second brain. TickTick is my go-to app for organizing everything from daily tasks to long-term goals. It seamlessly manages my to-do lists, reminders, and even helps me structure my projects with its simple but powerful interface. The calendar view is a lifesaver for planning ahead, and the ability to set recurring tasks keeps me on track with habits and routine tasks.

One feature I love is the habit tracker—it’s a real game-changer. Having a dedicated tool to track my habits within the same app means I don’t need a separate app to monitor my progress. This integration keeps everything in one place and keeps me motivated to stick with new habits.

The Eisenhower Matrix is also a huge plus, helping me effectively manage priorities. By categorizing tasks based on urgency and importance, I can focus on what truly matters and avoid getting bogged down by less critical items. If I could ask for one improvement, it would be the ability to create multiple Eisenhower Matrices—for example, one for personal tasks, another for family tasks, and a separate one for work. This addition would make task management even more flexible and organized.

The Pomodoro timer further supports my productivity, keeping me focused on each task at hand. And with tags and folders, finding my notes and tasks is quick and easy, perfect for busy days when I need information fast.

After four years of searching, I finally found TickTick. I needed a tool that could handle both my personal and professional life in all its forms—and TickTick is the only app I’ve come across that does this without being bulky. Data entry is quick and effortless, and the app is highly efficient. If it had just a touch of artificial intelligence to streamline workflows, it would be unbeatable. For anyone looking for a powerful yet lightweight productivity tool, TickTick is as good as it gets!

title: Pressuring users to sign up for an annual subscription
body: I’ve heard great things about this app, and I recently created an account. It has diverse features and a nice UI, so I’m looking forward to seeing how well I can get it to fit in with my workflow. However, during the onboarding/registration process the app prompts users to purchase an annual subscription, with no option to select a monthly term. What’s more, the option to close the prompt is fairly difficult to see, so it’s not immediately clear that you can continue without purchasing an annual subscription. It’s only by logging onto their website or going onto the App Store that you can select an option to purchase a monthly subscription, and even that isn’t very clear. I find tech companies that do these sorts of things to be shady and misleading. As a user, you shouldn’t have to jump through hoops or dig very deep to find and select the subscription term you want. What this tells me is that TickTick prioritizes profit over the user experience.

title: The missing piece in my ADHD life
body:
This app is amazing. Download it, subscribe, and let it change your life.

I have ADHD, and have long struggled with keeping on track at home. At work I have trackers and action registers, but nothing for home life. As such, my therapist suggested I try to replicate these. At first I tried to use Excel, then Microsoft To-Do, but found these lacked the functionalities I needed.

I had built my own task tracker for work, and had been adding functionalities for MONTHS. Was I ever going to find something that could deliver on these high standards?

Then I found this app. Oh. My. God. It’s a work of art. I subscribed early on to gain access to full features, and I am astonished at how it includes so much. At first glance it looks too simple, but all the features are there. Take the time to learn in, what each hold, tap, swipe can do, what’s hidden in the settings, etc.

So far all the things I had built into my own tracker for work I have found in this app. I foresee myself using this application for as long as I can

I will weep if this app over goes under. I have tasted true To Do list. 

There’s some minor things I’d love to see, and fully intend to submit suggestions via the website!

title: One App to Rule Them All
body: OMG this app is so good I had to write an essay about it. It does so many things but the interface is so clean, it’s kind of a design miracle. I can do everything I need in the free version but I subscribed because I want this app to exist forever. I have ADHD, so I’m always strategizing to manage my focus. Someone on an ADHD forum recommended TickTick and with some hesitation (oh no not another system…), I downloaded it a few weeks ago. I like productivity apps but if i have to flip between them, it’s not useful for me because … squirrel. TickTick has replaced the following apps for me: - ToDoist, Google Tasks - Done (habit tracker) - Toggl (task timer) - Notion (Notion is still awesome for many things, just not project management for my brain) - GoodNotes (ditto - still awesome, just not for tracking stuff) - and any number of timers and to-do lists TickTick takes my to-do list and puts the information in front of me when I need it. I can filter to just the things I need to immediately handle. I can set it to show me how long I have until the next thing is due (very helpful for a brain that only understands Now and Not Now.) It brings in my calendar events so I can see my days in context. I can start a Pomodoro (timed focus session) from within the task itself. It tracks habits and streaks, allowing me to write notes if I want to. When I reach a goal, it shows cute little animations that I like, (and I usually hate cute little animations.) And it’s got robust widgets, so good that I actually use the Apple Watch app. I actually use it on every device I own, iPad, Watch, Phone, as well as my PC via Chrome. Anyway if you are still reading, just get this app. It’s amazing. Thank you for coming to my Ted Talk.

title: Best to-do app on the market.  I’ve tried them all.
body:
This is without question the most intuitive to-do list app that I have used.  It’s different than anything else I’ve used and I have used them all ….believe me.  

A couple of things I think are really important… It’s visually intuitive with various views of your to-list that you can set up (I LOVE the Eisenhower Matrix view).  I also like the way that it does reminders, and the workflow is just very easy to understand. The amount of customization is impressive and continues to get better so there’s no limit to what you can do with this app.  And it’s stable.  Can’t stress how important this last point is. I’ve used a number of apps that crash once you get a fair amount of data, but these guys know how to build software.

I would recommend this to anybody that is looking to manage a large number of tasks that they need to get done both on the short term and long term.
I would give this more than 5 stars, if I could!

Thanks very much for a fantastic app. It’s been a game changer for me.

title: Academic with ADHD Approved!
body:
I’m a premed university student who was just diagnosed with ADHD and this helps me keep all my to-do’s, routine, and random thoughts all in one place! I wasn’t sure about this app at first because I didn’t know how to structure it for myself to work to my advantage. After getting a few ideas online, I’ve organized my task lists into folders depending on my needs. Free-trial definitely helped convince me to go with the pro version as the basic version lets you see your list for the day at a glance but as a visual person, seeing my month and weekly plan is a must! 
Time-management has always been elusive to me but TickTick has helped me structure my days to be productive and still fit in time for myself, my interests, and my loved ones.
Pomodoro feature helps me stay focused on my off-days when studying is the last thing I want to think about.
Many people like using multiple apps but having everything in one place for me to see and focus features really helps me ensure I’m not missing any upcoming due dates or tasks I want to complete!

Thank you TickTick for being so convenient and a godsend for helping me manage my ADHD!

title: Not accessible & priced out of reach
body: I’m getting annoyed with the inaccessible nature of apps. I wish apple would make it mandatory that any app sold through their AppStore had to be compatible with apple accessibility features. But here we are relying on app creators good nature to think about the fact that millions of people around the world live with a disability and rely on settings to make their phone accessible like large font and voiceover. Just make it compatible. I mean if you can code and create an app and push out updates periodically then I’m sure you’re smart enough to make it accessible. You could get millions of buyers and set yourself apart as an app that’s fully accessible, but instead we are excluded. Your app, unlike others , has a setting to increase font, except, that’s not to increase font for visually impaired people, it’s to increase font for sighted people to be more “comfortable”. The amount it increases the font size is a complete joke for a person with a visually impairment or who is legally blind. I hadn’t checked if your app is voiceover friendly so I won’t comment on that, but if you have chosen to only make it voiceover friendly and not large font friendly then that would be painting us all with the same brush and ignoring the fact that the majority of blind people have some amount of sight. You are but one of many many programmers who have a closed mind as to who makes up society.

body:
Although I have to confess that I am someone who bounces around with certain apps, ToDo/Reminder apps are one of them. I could probably make do with with just the Apple Reminders app, well since I retired, at work was a different matter.

So I have been through them all, and I will probably go through all the good ones again, with Things 2 being a go to, until I found TickTick.

I can live without some features if an app looks good, and TickTick looks darn good, BUT, it also has all the features I need. My only gripe our the widgets, and I don’t have an answer so maybe that the best that can be developed given the restraints that Apple put on developers, they just don’t look great and as I say I don’t know why. So, yeh, I may going back to Things 2 from time to time, but right now TickTick is my go to app and will probably be the one I will always go back to when I run around and try a different one just because it looked good.

Keep up the good work.

title: So much potential for power use but poor cross-platform implementation
body:
I'll start off by saying that this is a review of Tick Tick as a whole and not just the iOS version. I think that's important to note.

Overall, I had high hopes for Tick Tick. I thought it would have been a great cross platform option (I use a Windows device day-to-day for work) that would provide the power of GoodTask without the cost of something like OmniFocus. Unfortunately, Tick Tick proves that you can't have something Cheap, Functional, and Good Looking at the same time.

Instead of feeling like I am using a single service, each time I open one of Tick Tick's apps I feel like I'm in a completely different world. Yes, some features are only available on certain platforms due to ecosystem limitations, but that's not the problem. The problem is, the implementation of the same features on the different platforms are so widely different that I always found myself searching for a feature. It may be OK if you only ever use a single platform, but if you use more than one device you'll find yourself hunting for a feature/functionality OR having different results when using a feature. Something as simple as seeing what tasks are due on a given date is a dramatically different experience depending on what platform you're on. Like a game show, there’s always something different behind each door. 

There's also what seems like a language+logic problem. I am not certain where the app and it's developers are located, but I imagine it's not in an English first society. I mention this as the documentation and in-app explanations are not always the easiest to follow. Additionally, while these explanations are combined with the logic of the apps, the results of the functionality isn’t always as planned. 

I could likely rant about all of the small things that bother me about this app, and then rave about all of the things I like (not love). Unfortunately, the former accounts to much more than the latter.

I chose Tick Tick originally over Todoist as it had native apps—not just a web view; and seemed to offer the functionality that I’ve come to love about GoodTask. Unfrotauntely, because of the poor implemention of some very basic features, cross platform, I’ve had to throw in the towel on Tick Tick. I’ll likely revisit it near the year’s end to see if things have dramatically changed, but for now I’ll be sticking with Todist.

title: Finally... a full-featured integrated To Do and Calendar Solution
body:
TL/DR: If you’ve been looking for an app that combines a sophisticated To Do system with a full-featured calendar, look no further. TickTick has you covered. 

There’s lots of To Do apps out there and plenty of calendars, but nothing comes close to how this app merges both approaches to time and task management. Imagine if the iOS Reminders app showed each dated entry in the calendar app.  Then add tags, sub tasks and smart lists and you just beginning to get the idea of how well-designed TickTick is.  Follow GTD techniques?  No problem.  Like to use the Pomodoro Technique for task completion?  Check.  Yes, you will need to subscribe to premium for the full calendar functionality, but trust me... it’s worth it.  Using this mobile app along with its Mac version (which allows more sophisticated setup) is robust time and project management suite. 

The calendar is also full-featured with daily, 3-day, week, and month views. 

Sync between mobile and desktop is  instantaneous.  

Love. This. App.

title: Unreliable & inconvenient NPL
body:
Current Todoist user here. I’d been trying out TickTick because I like the idea of being able to replace my calendar app, pomodoro app, and habit tracking app with just this one app. I really enjoy the UI and the UX but I won’t be switching to TickTick (at least for now) and here is why:

PROS (because props where it’s due):

1) Clean, attractive, and modern UI: reminds me a lot of Things 3 but with the benefit of more functionalities.

2) Highly customisable Settings: I like how much control users are given over how they want the app to work and look for them.

3) Swipes on tasks: I like having Delete as one of the Swipe options so I can do it fast! Without having to do multiple clicks!

4) Pomodoro timer: looks good, customisable, works well. Definitely could replace pomodoro apps.

5) Calendar: pretty advanced too, since we get multiple views.

6) Habit tracker: looks good. Definitely could replace specific habit tracking apps.

7) Description and sub-tasks are on the main task view: I like that I only need to click once to access most the tasks’ details.

8) Cross-platform: yay to a Windows app!

9) Generous Free version: surprisingly a lot of functionalities offered are available for free like attachments, locations, tags, flags, and settings options. Usually a lot of those are only made available with a subscription in nearly all other apps.

10) Good and reasonable subscription fee: around 30$ is a really good annual price for an app that offers so much! I’d happily get it if I were to choose TickTick.

11) Can reorder tasks in today view: I like that views aren’t automatically ordered by time/priority. 

CONS:

1) Natural Language Processing when adding/editing tasks: I’m used to picking by typing in the task name—using convenient shorthands—the Priority, List name, and tags. In TickTick, doing all that is a lot slower because the symbols for those add-ons are not made available on the main keyboard. So I have to click more if I want to type, say, tags right into the task name.

Now the dealbreaker—the NLP doesn’t work well and is therefore unreliable. A lot of times, the subsequent add-on deactivates the previous add-on. For example, if I write “task #errands” then write “today at 1700”, the tag #errands turns into plain text (I.e. becomes part of task name) rather than staying registered as an added tag. 

2) Selecting all/multiple tasks requires too much clicking because I have to go to the menu at the top to get to “Edit Multiple” option. Would be better if I can press and hold onto any task in the list to activate multiple select.

3)No drag & drop: I can’t select, hold, and drag a task from one list into another.

title: TickTick, you complete me <3
body: I think it’s safe to say that I have tried nearly every productivity organization app in the app store and this is by far the best tool out there. Also, can we just talk about the built-in Pomo timer? And the time and productivity stats tracking? But TickTick can still have fun — they’ve built in just enough gamification to be playful and motivating but still serious about work. Are these guys for real? I thought I would never be satisfied with ANY app — but then TickTick showed up in my life and was like “Hey, girl.” And I was like “Oh, hai.” I always thought I would need a man to feel complete, but I was wrong. Every morning I wake up, roll over and check my phone and just knowing TickTick is wherever I need it (phone, iPad, desktop, web) makes me feel like everything is going to be okay. TickTick, you don’t just help me complete my tasks and projects, you complete me. Xo.

title: Cancelling is not possible, Only Renewal
body:

title: All around amazing app
body:
This app is awesome! Sleek design, great UI, super useful, customizable, organized and super easy to navigate! On top of that come features like the pomodoro counter, which are just super useful! I have the app on my mac too, and there've been no sync issues so far. This app completely decimates all competition (Microsoft to do etc.). 

Only thing that is missing would be a sort of “homework feature”, where you can enter a due date but plan on doing the task before its due. Maybe an option to create sub tasks with individual deadlines would be a solution? (Ex. essay due in one week, sub tasks: research on thursday and friday, outline on monday, writing the essay on tuesday and wednesday.) When sub tasks are completed, the main task is also automatically completed. Some sort of feature like that would really kick the greatness of this app into the stars.

Without an additional deadline feature I can’t put add the task to another day because that way I won’t know when it is due. This app would be the perfect app if I could add a deadline and a different date on which i want to complete the task. This is the only missing feature keeping me from switching from Things 3 to this App for good. 

The Pomodoro and calendar features are just amazing and so useful.

title: Ich liebe diese App
body:
TickTick ist für mich die perfekte All-in-One-Produktivitäts-App! Sie ist nicht nur ein Kalender, sondern auch ein großartiges Tool, um Routinen aufzubauen, Aufgaben zu organisieren und fokussiert zu arbeiten. Besonders gefällt mir der integrierte Pomodoro-Timer mit Statistiken – so behalte ich meine Arbeitszeiten immer im Blick.

Die Eisenhower-Matrix, die flexible Sortierung nach Tags oder Ordnern und die Möglichkeit, andere Kalender (z. B. den Apple-Kalender) zu importieren, machen die App extrem vielseitig. In der kostenpflichtigen Version kann man den Kalender in Listen-, Monats-, Tages-, 3-Tage- oder Wochenansicht gestalten – perfekt für jede Arbeitsweise.

Wiederholende Aufgaben, Priorisierung, Verknüpfungen zwischen Aufgaben, ortsbasierte Erinnerungen, Vorlagen, das Umwandeln von Aufgaben in Notizen – hier steckt so viel drin! Besonders praktisch finde ich auch, dass wichtige Aufgaben angepinnt werden können und im Sperrbildschirm live sichtbar sind, solange ich gerade daran arbeite. Und: Der Pomodoro-Fokus kann direkt aus einer Aufgabe heraus gestartet werden.

Früher brauchte ich mehrere separate Apps für Timer, Routinen, Kalender und Aufgaben – jetzt habe ich alles in einer einzigen, intuitiven App. Absolut empfehlenswert!

title: Feature editable
body:
Hi team! 
I've been using the app for almost a year now. And its been great. Since i recently use the podomoro and focus feature, i think would be nice if we can edit the time we took, because sometimes, i forgot to stop the timer and just close my laptop, and in the morning i got asked how long did i worked, instead of the time. And that is one thing. One other thing, so for that i just put number right. Like 8hours. But later then when i have time, i checked my other note, i worked more than 8 hours and i go back to the podomoro and wanted to change the hour but i cant. So, would be nice if we can edit the time, and not askd for how long (because the you ask the user to count, and its not efficient) better ask what time did you finish or something.

Apart from that. I like the app very much! Awesome ✨

title: Datenschutz verbessern! Projektmanagement-Möglichkeiten verbessern
body: Der Datenschutz geht leider garnicht! Bitte Analyse der Daten mit selbst überlassen oder zumindest opt-out-Möglichkeit bieten. WICHTIG WÄRE: Standard-Einstellung für Kalenderansicht (also Standard z.B. auf „7 Tage“ stellen zu können, statt immer Manuel das umstellen zu müssen). Ebenso: Es wäre schön, wenn ihr die Möglichkeit hinzufügen könntet, dass man, wenn man bspw. Projekte hat, die sich wiederholen und immer bspw. über 6 Wochen gehen, diese 1. Im Kalender auch alle untereinander anzuzeigen (bis zu 10 Stk um die Übersicht zu wahren, wann welches Projekt zu Ende ist, beginnt etc.). Ebenso dass man dann für so ein Standardprojekr gleich „Standarderinnerungen“ einstellt, um dies nicht immer und immer wieder einzeln einstellen zu müssen Weiterhin toll wäre: Möglichkeit im Kalender einstellen zu können, dass man alle Ganztages-Termine auch untereinander anzeigen lassen kann, bislang werden maximal 4-5 untereinander angezeigt Ansonsten wirklich tolle App!

title: Tolle To-do App mit Sicherheitsdefiziten
body: Die App hat viele Features, die ich in anderen To-do Apps bislang vermisst habe, z.B. Prioritäten nach Eisenhauer Matrix setzen, Ziele verfolgen können und Gewohnheiten systematisch in den Tagesablauf integrieren. Alle Features funktionieren sofort, wie erwartet und vieles ist im Detail gut gelöst. Man merkt, dass die Nutzererfahrung einen extrem hohen Stellenwert bei der Entwicklung hat. Was ich allerdings schmerzlich vermisse, sind für mich wichtige Sicherheitsfeatures, die den Datenschutz betreffen. Dazu zählen Ende zu Ende Verschlüsselung bei der Datenübertragung zu den Servern sowie eine Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung. Das sind für mich in den heutigen Zeiten selbstverständliche Features.

body: Auf dem Handy finde ich die App großartig. Man kann alles tun, was man mit einer Todo-App können will. Des Weiteren gibt es eine Möglichkeit, Einträge aus der Erinnerungen-App zu importieren, um Siri nutzen zu können und trotzdem alle seine Todos in Tick Tick zu haben (Integration ohne explizites Importieren gibt es im Pro-Abo). Was mich jedoch stört, ist, dass die App den Platz auf dem iPad nicht ausnutzt. Die Seitenleiste, in der die verschiedenen Listen stehen, könnte die ganze Zeit sichtbar sein, sodass man sich ständiges Gewische sparen würde. Genug Platz ist jedenfalls da, anders als auf dem Handy. Wenn das noch implementiert ist, gibt es den 5. Stern!

title: Einfach wow!
body:
Ich habe alle großen Player der To-Do-Apps durchprobiert, war jahrelang Nutzer von Omnifocus, Things, Sorted, u. a. und habe ebenfalls Collaboration-Tools wie Trello für meine Projektorganisation genutzt und ausprobiert.
Doch TickTick ist wie wie der heilige Gral und vereint alle guten Eigenschaften sämtlicher Tools. Bei für mich maximal komfortabler Bedienung mit der höchst möglichen Flexibilität. Versch. Ansichten inkl. Eisenhower, Zeitstrahl und Kanban, dazu Pomodorotimer und Habittracker. Dazu Aufgabenverteilung im Team, Notizen anlegen usw. Das ist wirklich absolute Königsklasse und ganz großes Kino.

title: Überzeugt mich überhaupt nicht
body: Es ist eine brauchbare Todo Liste, auch der Pomodoro Timer ist ok. Was mir aber komplett fehlt ist eine Funktion die bei Aktivierung des Pomodoro Timers das nicht stören des Smartphones einschaltet. Es hilft überhaupt nicht wenn man konzentriert arbeiten möchte, während der Zeit aber laufend Mitteilungen eintreffen die das Handy signalisiert. Damit ist die Konzentration vorbei. Am besten wäre eine Funktion die  wählbaren Apps die Benachrichtigung verbietet, so daß nur bestimmte Apps ihre Mitteilung senden dürfen, alle anderen aber nicht. Mit Ende des Pomodoro Timer sollten dann wieder alle Apps Benachrichtigungen senden dürfen. Solange das nicht der Fall ist, werde ich diese App nicht nutzen können. Tut mir leid.

body:
Keine Synchronisation über die iCloud

Im Kalender von TickTick sieht man seiner Termine, aber man sieht kein Start- oder Enddatum einer Aufgabe im lokalen Apple-Kalender.
Wieder soll ich den Google-Kalender nutzen. Was sollen meine Kalenderdaten bei Google?
Ohne die „echte“ iCloud-Synchro fehlt die Verbindung zu meinem lokalen Kalender und damit zum Kalender meiner Partnerin.
Nicht für das Geld!

title: Zu Unrecht oft übersehen….
body: Denn diese App ist fantastisch und sollte viel öfter auftauchen in den Suchergebnissen. Endlich vereinen sich auf zuverlässige Weise Termine, todos und Gewohnheiten in einer App! Endlich auf eine wirklich gelungene und übersichtliche Weise! Auch die Eisenhower Matrix ist jetzt ein tolles Feature um das Wichtigste im Blick zu behalten! Unteraufgaben können eigene Erinnerungen bekommen… von allen Geräten aus kann ich zugreifen ohne extra kosten für die Desktop Variante. Die Synchronisation läuft besser als bei vielen anderen! Gmail Erweiterung und co… was will man mehr und das für den kleinen Preis! So toll ehrlich! Ich liebe auch die Möglichkeit auf den Laptop die kanban Style Variante du wählen als Ansicht! Und bei den Gewohnheiten nutze ich teils die „Check in“ Option und habe so ein Mini Journal mit dabei gleich…. Nachdem ich mit wirklich (fast?) alle vergleichbaren Apps zum Thema über Jahre angeschaut habe, ist dies bisher mein absoluter Favorit! Es lohnt sich 👍 tolle Arbeit!

title: Die Eisenhower-Matrix ist überragend
body:
Ich fand die App schon vor der Eisenhower-Matrix super, da ich unbedingt eine Priorisierung, sowie eine Kategorisierung unterschiedlicher Tasks brauche. Seit die App auch noch die Eisenhower-Matrix-Anzeige unterstützt ist sie für mich unersetzbar. 

Ich würde die Entwickler wirklich gerne finanziell unterstützen, finde die App allerdings sehr teuer. Für das TeacherTool beispielsweise bezahlte ich einmalig 30 € und hierfür 25 € pro Jahr? TeacherTool berechnet, verwahrt, verschlüsselt Noten von Schüler*innen. Die Verantwortung hierbei ist viel größer als das Aufgabengebiet von TickTick. Der hohe Preis erschließt sich mir leider nicht. Man merkt: Ich bin Lehrer. Gibt es eine Education-Lizenz?

Mit der kostenlosen Variante fahre ich soweit auch ganz gut. Eine Kleinigkeit wäre allerdings wichtig für mich: „urgent and important“ sollte überfällige ToDos enthalten. Überfällige ToDos sind doch wichtiger als ToDos von Morgen, oder nicht?

Trotzdem: 5 Sterne. Sensationelles Tool! Vielen Dank an die Entwickler.

title: Hype nicht nachvollziehbar
body:
Ich hatte die App runtergeladen, weil sie von Apple angeteasert wurde und überall gehyped wird. Ist für mich nicht nachvollziehbar. 

 Zunächst mal fehlt der voreingestellte automatische Darkmode. Wenn das ganze Handy dunkel eingestellt ist, dann ist das Öffnen dieser App keine Freude: schmerzhaft grell und kontrastarm, sehr schwierig zu bedienen mit Sehbehinderung. Setzt euch mal bitte mit Barrierefreiheit auseinander. 

Die Lokalisierung ist eine Katastrophe! Ein Mischmasch aus Englisch und Deutsch, die Übersetzungen sind oft unverständliches Kauderwelsch. Übersetzungen gehören in die Hände von Profis. Sonst ist das nur peinlich. 

Die Bedienung ist nicht intuitiv. Altbackenes und unübersichtlich Layout überfrachtet mit Funktionen, die Sprachverwirrung machts nicht besser. Man muss sich in alles ewig reinfuchsen, nicht gut für ein Werkzeug, das die Produktiv erhöhen soll, wenn sie selbst zum Zeitfresser wird. Ich glaube nicht, dass ich damit warm werde.

Edit: lol no, I'm not willing to help develop a product that I paid for. Fun fact: When I go to a restaurant, I don't cook there myself. The translations in the app are exactly the quality you get if you are not willing to pay a professional translator: very poor. On the other hand, your customers expect high quality for paying YOU. Think about it!

title: Beste Todo-App
body:
Ich beschäftigte mich seit über 20 Jahren intensiv mit Produktivität und kann folgendes sagen: 

TickTick versteht wie Produktivität und effektives Aufgaben- und Zeitmanagement und GTD wirklich funktioniert. Daher verbindet TickTick in einem Tool gekonnt das was man dafür braucht: Aufgaben, Kalender, Habits, Focus Timer, Notizen und noch einiges mehr zwar gut aufeinander abgestimmt. So kann man endlich verschiedene Apps mit einem ersetzen und hat einen viel besseren Überblick. 

Mit jedem Update bin ich noch begeisterter von TickTick, nicht nur, weil hier schnell und kontinuierlich weiter entwickelt wird, sondern auch weil genau das geliefert wird was man anfragt und als Nutzer wirklich haben will und braucht. 

Endlich keine App die nur auf Design und Schein achtet, sondern einem wirklich helfen will produktiver und fokussierter zu sein. Wenn es so weiter geht werden alle bekannten Todo Apps bald überholt. Macht bitte weiter so!

Ich bin positiv überrascht! Die App ist extrem Nutzerfreundlich und ich kann sie insgesamt tatsächlich anstandslos empfehlen. Kompliment!

Einen klaren Punktabzug gibt es aber Pricing: Wir sind sechs Leute und es gibt offenbar keinerlei Angebote/Mengenrabatt für Teams! Lediglich einen Monat gratis für eine Weiterempfehlung — womit man nichts anfangen kann.

title: Noch nicht perfekt
body:
Ich bin erst vor kurzem auf Tick Tick gestoßen und habe alle anderen To-Do-Apps auch bereits getestet. Tick Tick gefällt mir gut, aber es könnten auch einige Dinge noch verbessert werden, um wirklich gut damit arbeiten zu können.

1) die deutsche Übersetzung (vor allem auf dem Mac)
2) die Ansicht von mehreren Projekten in einem Ordner: Warum muss ich auf ein Element innerhalb des Ordners „Alle Aufgaben“ klicken und es erscheinen nicht alle Aufgaben, wenn ich auf den Ordner selbst klicke/tippe?
3) warum können entweder Beschreibungen oder Checklisten, nicht aber beides hinzugefügt werden?
4) echte Unteraufgaben wären ohnehin praktischer
5) Einige Design-Kleinigkeiten für mehr Übersicht

body: Arbeite beruflich seit Jahren mit todo Apps und beschäftige mich gerne mit der Optimierung meiner Aufgabenorganisation. Aus diesem Grund habe ich über die Jahre fast alle Apps ausprobiert. Viele sind prima unter iOS und MAC, aber nur wenige schaffen den Spagat zwischen den Systemen. Tick Tick schafft das fast perfekt. In den letzten Monaten kommen immer mehr Apps mit integrierten Kalendern auf den Markt. Das ist genial und auch hier kann Tick Tick unter MAC und iOS mithalten. Nur unter Windows ist die Kalenderintegration noch nicht anständig möglich (Exchangeserver) - typisch Windows. Die Bedienung ist Top, die Ansichtmöglichkeiten sind perfekt. Der Sync ist schnell und korrekt.

title: Gute App, leider mit Abo
body:
Die App ist super praktisch, um alles mögliche festzuhalten oder zu planen und am Ende abzuhaken. Sie ist sehr übersichtlich und intuitiv, aber sie hat meiner Meinung nach einen nicht gerechtfertigten Preis, was die „pro“ Funktionen angeht. Ich möchte nicht für jede App die ich benutze ein Abo abschließen. Für ca. 3 Euro im Monat oder 30€ pro Jahr weiche ich dann doch lieber auf konkurrierende Apps aus, die nur einmalig etwas kosten. Für einmalige 10-15€ wäre ich bereit eine „pro“ Version zu kaufen, aber nicht für den doppelten Preis und dann auch noch jedes Jahr.

Ich kritisiere jegliche Art von Abomodellen bei neuerdings jeder möglichen App. Apps sind kleine Hilfsmittel, die einem das Leben leichter machen sollen. Wenn ich für jede App, die ich nutze, ein Abo abschließen müsste, um sie im vollen Umfang nutzen zu können, wäre man bei über 100€ im Monat. Das wiederum wirkt ja dem Sinn einer App entgegen. Gegen einen einmaligen Preis, der gerechtfertigt ist (10-15€), habe ich nichts einzuwenden, da schließlich die Entwickler der App auch nicht umsonst arbeiten wollen.

Wenn das Abomodell verschwindet, bekommt die App von mir 5*, so leider nur 3*.

It is the better version of Todoist with additional features and a far superior UX both for iOS and Mac.

It has everything Todoist offers, filters, dates, tags and project parsing plus:

- It has an embedded Pomo Timer (time management to stay focused)
- Calendar (once you create tasks you can arrange tasks directly with the embedded calendar
- Percentage for tasks
- UX and smooth App both for iPad, iphone and Mac

Please give it a shot guys and you won’t regret it

title: Love the app ❤️, but a request if I may?
body:
My favorite app as it enables voice memos, audio attachments, timer, and calendar in one :)! Only one I’ve found that does all of that by itself!

Some concerns;
1. When I add an attachment to “repeat daily” tasks, it duplicates them across all the days. Which can be forever… Can you make it so that the attachments don’t duplicate and stay individual? Or at least as an option? 

2. Don’t know if this is on purpose or not, but when template adds to folder and I moves it again to another folder, it deletes the root template task and all the subtasks become tasks.

Also an idea;
Option to add timer to tasks. You can press a button on a task and it starts counting based on ‘individual task timer settings’ decided on. And when timer ends task gets automatically completed.
Perhaps also to habits.

Best of wishes,
From me

title: A lot like Apple Reminders in design but better
body: TickTick has become my friend over the past couple of months. I was very used to Apple Reminders on my devices, so it was difficult to try something new, which was not automatically integrated in iCloud services. Normally that would be an issue to me due to the lack of simplicity, but the features which are packed in the app TickTick does a difference. Take the behavioral feature called “Habits”, it has completely changed my mindset towards things I need to become better at. Right now my focus is to drink more water, because I feel demotivated completing my tasks when I’m dehydrated. It has helped me a lot by using such an integrated feature. The reason why I’m not providing full stars in my review is, that I believe dark mode should be a complementary feature these days, and I would also like to see a board like view as we can have in an app like Trello. Combining Project boards with Reminders would be the absolute go to app for me personally.

title: The best
body:
I am truly impressed with the features of TickTick and the way they've been packed nicely into a great interface.
I'm not paying, it's expensive for me as a student, and generally I dislike monthly payment (if there was an affordable one time fee I'd buy it), but the free features are plenty so I'm very happy with that so far.
One specific feature I was looking for was a "blank canvas" every day while still having yesterday's and all the other day's undone to-do's easily and clearly accessed when wanted. It's actually a rare feature and was what I liked a lot about Microsoft Todo, while that's a pretty poor experience otherwise, so I'm glad I found one that has that plus everything I missed from MS. I've used maaaany task managers, they play a big role in my everyday, and Ticktick makes them all look like toys.

title: Muy buena app, pero le falta un detalle clave en los hábitos
body:
TickTick es excelente para organizar tareas, gestionar proyectos y mantener el enfoque. Me encanta su diseño, la posibilidad de crear hábitos y la funcionalidad del calendario. Sin embargo, hay un punto importante que limita la organización: los hábitos no se reflejan en el calendario como sí lo hacen las tareas.

Esto genera confusión, ya que muchos hábitos tienen un horario específico y al no verse en la agenda, uno puede pensar que tiene ese tiempo libre, cuando en realidad está reservado. Esto afecta la planificación diaria, especialmente para quienes buscamos integrar hábitos a una rutina con horarios bien definidos.

📌 Recomendación: Sería muy útil que los hábitos pudieran visualizarse en el calendario según el horario asignado. Incluso como un bloque opcional o en un color distinto para diferenciarlos de las tareas, pero que estén visibles en la vista de agenda.

Si integran esto, ¡sería una herramienta prácticamente perfecta!

title: a very versatile, complete app
body:
However I do have a couple of notes about what could be improved.
Indentation (➡️tab) on task/notes description would be very cool.
Whenever you open a folder, you can’t select the list you want to add a task to, you have to select it from the left menu or write “~list”. This is inconvenient since “~” takes a while to find.
A third type of list (additional to “task” or “notes”) could be really useful; one that is previewed with images and serves as a “moodboard”.
It would also be nice to be able to see the tasks inside a task by “unfolding” it the way you do lists, without having to open it up.
I think the “reward system” for completing tasks is great, I would expand the unlockable benefits way more (like new sounds for pomodoro, etc).
Lastly it would be nice to have another type of habit, a “quitting” type; where it autocompletes as positive unless you interact with it.
All of these are ideas I’ve thought of while using it, nonetheless it’s an amazing app for how little it costs. :-)

title: Potencia, flexibilidad y simplicidad
body:
Llevo años (sin exagerar) probando apps que se adapten a mi workflow y vida personal. 
He probado muchísimas apps (Todoist, Omnifocus, 2do, Things...). Unas muy complejas, otras muy caras, otras poco flexibles, otras demasiado simples...
Uno de los requisitos que necesitaba era la posibilidad de añadir a una tarea fecha de inicio y fin, a veces puedo tardar más de un día en completarla. TickTick cuenta con esta función y otras muchas que han hecho que en una semana sea un imprescindible.

Todabía no le he encontrado ninguna pega, permite acceder desde cualquier plataforma mediante web, tiene apps muy cuidadas para iOS, iPadOS, MacOS y WatchOS❤️. 
También cuenta con la función de reconocimiento de fechas y horas (Todoist style), añadir tareas de forma rápida por dictado, crear carpetas de proyectos, comentarios en task, adjuntar archivos, vista calendario, formato kanban, listas intelgentes...

La sincronización es perfecta entre dispositivos. Añado una tarrea para hoy desde macOS y a los 2 segundos aparece en la compilación de mi Apple Watch.

Gracias por vuestro excelente trabajo.

Además, en las últimas actualizaciones habéis hecho un cambio muy a peor, la ventana de estadísticas era mucho mejor antes. En las versiones anteriores se podían ver sin conexión a internet y la gráfica permitía mostrar la información exacta mes a mes, sabiendo exactamente el número de tareas realizadas durante el mes. title: À fuir ! Arnaque à l’essai gratuit !!
body:
À fuir. Arnaque à l’essai gratuit.
J’ai téléchargé l’application en pensant bénéficier d’une version d’essai (DC) pour évaluer les fonctionnalités. Résultat : au 6e jour, prélèvement automatique de 39 €, sans alerte préalable, sans moyen de contact fiable, et aucun remboursement possible via Apple.

L’app est basique, décevante, largement inférieure à des outils sérieux comme Calendars ou OmniFocus, pourtant proposés au même tarif. Interface peu ergonomique, fonctionnalités limitées, promesses non tenues.

Les avis positifs semblent douteux : soit achetés, soit postés par des utilisateurs peu exigeants. Cette maison d’édition donne l’impression de manquer d’éthique autant que de moyens. Je déconseille fortement.
author: Mona75016

title: Application excellente mais...
body:
L'application en elle-même est super, mais attention à n'avoir aucun problème de connexion n'activez pas la double authentification. À cause de cela je me suis retrouvé dans l'impossibilité de récupérer mon compte et le support client est quasiment inexistant. Ils répondent une fois sur dix et n'apporte aucune solution. Résultat j'ai payé un abonnement pour 1 an dont j'ai pu profiter que quelques mois et j'ai bien sûr perdu toutes mes données aux passages. Tout ça car je voulais mieux sécurisé mes données, un comble ! 

Ce qui m'amène à deux défauts majeurs, on ne m'y reprendra plus : la gestion des données qui n'est pas en local et très limités. Également la gestion des notes en elle-même en terme d'UX et fonction n'est vraiment pas très bonne. 

Je suis repassé sur note plan qui est bien plus flexible et clair. Il n'y a pas l'aspect focus, stats, c'est un peu plus austère, mais je suis sur d'avoir le contrôle sur mes donnée et l'intégration intelligente de l'ia, une mellleur visibilité des objectif long terme et de la prise de note, des rappels, événements ect, tout ceci fait que c'est finalement bien supérieure à Tick Tick et surtout plus fiable sur le long terme.

title: Je l’adore
body:
Ça fait un moment que je l’utilise et je le ferai encore pour longtemps je crois. C’est un des applis les plus modulables et complètes avec des améliorations continues. 

Quelques idées pour le futur ;
- J’aimerais bien que la synchronisation avec les calendriers soit meilleure. Dans mon expérience, surtout avec Outlook, les événements sont bien importées la première fois mais quand il y a des changements soit coté TickTick soit coté Outlook la synchronisation ne semble pas bidirectionnelle. Si on veut utiliser que TickTick pour organiser notre vie personnelle et professionnelle, donc avoir tout dans le même endroit, la synchronisation doit être fiable et bidirectionnelle. 
- je trouverai aussi très utile que un événement d’un calendrier externe comme Outlook soit traitable comme une tache. Donc que je puisse appuyer sur « compléter » et que puisse disparaître du calendrier quand fait. Ça permettrait une gestion plus complète et propre des tâches quotidiennes. 
- dernièrement j’utilise beaucoup le minuteur pompdoro, et je préfère parfois me concentrer avec ma musique à moi. Ça serait très utile de pouvoir choisir comme son du minuteur sa propre musique au lieu de celle proposée. 

C’est comme même très bien.

title: + qu’utile
body:
Cette application ouvre la porte à une nouvelle vie si vous savez comment vous fixer des objectifs. 

Que vous soyez salariés ou entrepreneur, je vous la recommande parce que, 

La matrice d’Eisenhower est une arme ultime pour les gens multitâche!
Le système pomodoro est plus qu’appréciable, j’en fais souvent usage pour ma part et ça structure mon temps d’une manière fluide. 

Les moins, si vous travaillez sur plusieurs appareils l’application a un temps de réponse lent (voir inexistant parfois) lorsqu’il s’agit de mettre sur pause le pomodoro. Ça reste accessoire mais ça serait bien de l’implanter dans le futur. 

Merci pour cette application remplie de sens.

title: Application sous coté
body:
Tick tick est une très bonne application tant dans sa simplicité que ça polyvalence bien que malheureusement je dois en complément utilisé Notion car l’application parfaite n’existe pas encore que ce soit pour du suivie de projet plus détaillé mon suivi de budget et mes notes par contre Tick tick apporte ça force dans l’intégration de tâches au calendrier, l’abonnement possible et fluide d’apple calendrier et google calendrier. Le système d’habitude qui est très simple et très bien fait beaucoup mieux que notion selon mes critères. Un pomodoro pratique et enfin la matrice d’Eisenhower.

L’abonnement est raisonnable pour un an d’utilisation, cela fait moins de 3,5€/mois et pour le confort qu’elle apporte je dis oui.

Pour l’équipe développement il serait intéressant de pouvoir choisir via l’onglet calendrier quels calendrier choisir plutôt que de devoir épingler les différents calendrier et de devoir sortir du calendrier pour ensuite ajouter manuellement. 

Pour les notes la possibilité de mettre des tableaux serait plus confortable ainsi que des notes audio. Rapprocher vous de apple notes qui est une très bonne applications de note toujours dans le même esprit que le votre « la simplicité » J’espère que mes explications seront claires et j’espère que vous arriverez à thermes à être le Notion mais simple comparé à ce dernier qui nécessite un gros temps d’adaptation

title: Excellente application, la meilleure de son genre
body:
Utilisateur depuis plusieurs années, cette application est une de mes indispensables.

Seul regret : même si elle est extrêmement complete, au bout de 3-4 ans d’usage en version gratuite, j’ai été confronté à des limites de la version gratuite (qui est déjà extrêmement complète), dans le nombre de création des taches affectée à une catégorie (100 taches maximum par catégorie).

De fait, j’utilise maintenant un outil moins user friendly, qui n’a pas été créé pour cet usage, mais qui est beaucoup plus polyvalent et sans aucune limitation (Notion).

2 regrets dont 1 qui est commun à toutes les applications Saas :
- l’impossibilité d’acheter une licence perpétuelle, l’abonnement reste la seule option possible pour utiliser toutes les fonctionnalités de l’application. Personnellement je ne veux pas dun abonnement supplémentaire, j’aurais préféré rétribuer l’entreprise une fois même s’il faut mettre le prix
- le flou quand à la gestion des données personnelles par l’entreprise tierce (chiffrement, gestion, hébergement onpremise ou cloud ?), on ne connaît rien du stockage de nos données et de leur gestion. Mais ce dernier point est commun à toutes les applications du genre.

Un énorme merci à l’équipe pour le travail effectué : cette application est une bombe, et le service client est très sympa, réactif et efficace !

title: Application complète, oui comme...
body: ...Une usine à gaz ! On peu tout faire ou presque, mais au prix de nombreuses manipulations que l’on n’imagine même pas faire face à un ami ou une relation pour noter rapidement un événement avec force détails ! Ex : Il y a des tags, très bien mais, pourquoi ne sont-ils pas accessibles pendant la saisie de l’événement ? Mes événements sont tous marqués de la même couleur dans la visualisation du calendrier général (?) bien que, issus de calendriers partagés de couleurs différentes ? Pour mon point de vue, les paramètres d’un événement se traitent au moment de la saisie de l’événement. Sinon, perte de temps ! L’ergonomie, il faut trop souvent le rappeler est, faire le plus intuitivement possible, un maximum de choses en un minimum de manipulations ! Objectif non atteint ici par rapport à d’autres applications ! J’ai acheté l’application, j’espère trouver des raisons de changer mon opinion ! Addentum : Des couleurs pour les calendriers, oui ! Mais, ça reste, en général, très redondant !

title: Le top... ET ENFIN EN FRANÇAIS !
body:
Dernière mise à jour (mi-décembre 2018) historique ! Ça y est TickTick parle français (à activer dans les paramètres) !

——

Depuis plus de 10 ans j’ai à peu près tout testé (et payé pour beaucoup), aussi bien des « petites » applis de gestion des tâches que celles ayant pignon sur rue (dans le désordre Omnifocus, Informant, Todoist, Things, 2Do, MyLifeOrg, Toodledo, Todo, Gneo, LifeTopix ... la liste n’est pas exhaustive). J’ai alterné entre les uns et les autres durant quelques mois, un an... j’ai même fait des allers-retours. Et à la fin il y avait toujours la frustration d’avoir 80% de ce qui me fallait mais jamais la totalité. 
Omnifocus : pas de vrai calendrier, gestion des tâches répétitives insatisfaisante, plateforme synchronisée sur Mac et iPad uniquement. 
Informant : Usine à gaz. Synchronisations complexes. 
Todoist : pas de calendrier 
2Do : un peu compliqué, pas de calendrier, plateforme synchronisée sur Mac et iPad 
uniquement. 
Things : un peu limité, pas de calendrier, plateforme synchronisée sur Mac et iPad 
uniquement. 
Avec TickTick, j’ai enfin trouvé une appli efficace, permettant de traiter aussi bien  les petites tâches simples que les plus gros projets. L’intégration calendrier est le gros point fort. On peut faire naviguer les tâches au milieu des rdv avec une grande facilité. L’interface est simple et pourtant on peut faire beaucoup de chose : dossiers et tags, multisélection, partages, intégrations de photos, enregistrements et autres fichiers, sous-tâches, répétitions de tâche, gestion des rappels, intégration Siri... Pas de bug, pas de « lag » de synchronisation, multiplateforme avec une synchronisation irréprochable et automatique. Que du bon. Certes pour accéder à toutes les fonctions il faut passer par un abonnement mais franchement je suis heureux de payer 2 ou 3 euros par mois pour pouvoir enfin utiliser un outil réellement productif. Le seul regret : pas encore en Français. Mais j’ai bon espoir : j’ai très largement participé à la traduction en français qui vient tout juste d’être terminée et il ne reste plus à l’équipe de TickTick que de l’intégrer dans une prochaine mise à jour. J’espère que ça ne sera pas trop long.

title: Superb GTD app
body:
I tried pretty much every (free and premium) task management apps and TickTick is a super clean, flexible and ubiquitous solution to get things done. 

I can set a day or a specific reminder which is a great in between (what Things and OmniFocus lack). Plus TickTick is available on every platforms. 

As a standalone free app, there's no real limitation which is truly a great improvement compared to both Wunderlist and Todoist — we are fermium and both available everywhere. 

The design is a mix between Things and Todoist, without the complexity of OmniFocus and the ability to tap a task and see the note (literally like a note taking app) is… wow. 

I may not need a subscription as of now but I'll get one anyway, that app just feels so great.

TickTick allows me to continually chart my work progress with free flowing text plus photos, links and documents. Of course it offers reminders, categories, analyses, pomodoro timers etc

I also use Asana, Trello and OneNote, but I found the speed and customisability of TickTick allows me to be productive without getting in the way.

Whenever I have problems or bugs the developers are quick to respond and identify and fix the issue.

Right now, living without it would be difficult so I rate it as an excellent application.

title: Brilliant app - wish I could pay a one-off fee for life.
body:
I just started using it and it’s honestly brilliant. It’s incredibly feature-rich, giving you plenty in free mode, while also offering substantial extras for premium mode. For me, the game changer is the Eisenhower Matrix. I’m really bad for doing things that aren’t a priority at the expense of other things even though I keep a bullet journal for my tasks. When my days are hectic I’m usually pretty good, but on the less hectic days, this is where I go astray. Having an editable EM is a revelation for me and elevates the app above all others, and it will work perfectly with my bullet journal.

I tried a few other big name apps, which all give free versions, but they’re so limited that they’re simply not workable in the free version. They all provide trials, like TickTick, but I uninstalled them without using the free trial. A free workable version, that still keeps some goodies for premium, and is really good will make me want to buy it, simply because it’s so good and because the developers are so generous with what they provide. However, none of them provide the EM. 

I have one single gripe and it’s a wider gripe for most services these days, but there’s no lifetime fee. I’m fed up with subscriptions because they all add up every month.  Tick Tick is actually a tiny subscription, especially compared to others, so it’s definitely worth paying for but it’d be nice to have the option to buy it outright too, offering the developer team some security as well. Otherwise, I can’t praise this app highly enough.

title: Incomparable to every other todo list app
body: I have used every todo list app I can get my hands on. Well, hands down this is the best todo list app I have ever used. I can’t believe how well the logic behind the app works! Not only does it have options that toggle to become exactly what I am looking for, it’s so customizable that you can get it to work the way you work. Do you need things to be in different lists? Done. Do you need due dates? Finished. Repeat by due date finished or date complete? Can’t believe I have never seen it before. I am not exaggerating: I was so frustrated that I was setting out to program my own todo list app so that I can finally get the features I want. Well, guess what? Now I am more than happy to have to pay for it! It has about 90% overlap with the functionality that I was wanting for my own app. And they take feedback seriously. I already had one of my suggestions passed onto the development team! And don’t worry, TickTick, I have plenty more to send your way. I’ll just be sure to have it on a separate list with tags and a repeating every two weeks task to keep it from overstaying my welcome! 5/5 stars, never looking again, finally.

title: The best!
body:
I have never written an app review, but absolutely had to for this one!

I have tried various to-do list and focus apps before, but always found them to have too many ‘extra’ things that have nothing to do with the main purpose of the app. TickTick is simple, effective and cuts straight to the point - which is exactly what I wanted from a focus app.

The list and sub-list option is so useful, especially as a student who has to constantly keep track of different tasks for different subjects, course modules and exams. 

One of the biggest pros about this app is having a focus timer and a to-do list in one app which can be seamlessly linked together and are presented in a simple, easy layout. Not to mention the focus statistics that are provided, which are so good for keeping track of how much time is spent on each aspect.

I would 100% recommend this app to anyone looking to make life a little bit easier!

Well done to the app developers. I am grateful for your hard work! :) 10/10 - would definitely recommend!

title: Amazing Organisational Tool
body:
This app works really well at being an excellent tool for to do lists, and organising your life! I use it as both a standard to do list, and essentially a calendar. Instead of having a calendar and having to click into every individual day to see what is planned, I use Tick Tick to schedule the days in advance and so I know even at a swift glance what I’m up to on a certain date! 

This app also works well for giving further detail to the to do list or bulleted item. You can add notes or images to the entry, which is really helpful, for example I normally add an entry when I know I am going into the city, and will then use the image note feature to save a picture of the train time table with the entry which is really useful. 

You can also make recurring events such as weekly tasks, which is a great feature, and you can tag and separate your tasks too into work, home, normal etc. I love the time and urgency feature in which you can tag how urgent it is, and what time it should alert you to the task as a notification if necessary. 

All of this is on the free version, and I find it’s very functional and the best organisational app I have found so far! It does everything that I need and all in one easy place, been using this app for over 2 years now and I’ve certainly tried, tested, and loved it!

title: Excellent app that just works and makes your life easier
body:
I previously had a to do list in notes, a habits app and a physical diary. I mainly kept a physical diary as I don’t like to be hooked to my phone.

TickTick has simplified my set up and has led to less procrastination.

I love that your habits, daily to do list and calendar are in one easy to navigate location. You also still get the positive affect of ticking of your to do list and at the end of the day you can see how productive you have been.

Eisenhower matrix for your to do list is also a helpful feature. You can have a to do list here that has not yet been allocated to a day for action and you can also list tasks based on importance.

It’s worth ever penny and getting rid of my physical diary has actually been a positive move. 

I personally like to turn of all notifications in TickTick, as I find all these phone notifications contribute to being hooked on your phone and lead to anxiety/stress. 

A big thanks to MKHBD for recommending this app in your YouTube video.
