title: Best out there
body: I never leave reviews but I just have to for this app. This is everything I was looking for! Originally, I was put off by the ‘In-App Purchases’ disclaimer as so many apps are virtually unusable without a subscription, but the features offered FOR FREE by this app are phenomenal, with no ads! And it’s so affordable if you’re willing to pay! I searched for so long for a To Do list app that was useful for deadlines and offered both an overview and a deep dive into tasks that had to be done, as well as sub-tasks,  and this is that very app. I love how customisable it is  — sort tasks into personalised lists, add tags to find them easily, rearrange the sidebar to your liking, set sub-tasks OR checklists, assign emojis and colours to your lists, put lists in folders or add sections to your lists. The app comes with sections to see what’s coming up Today, Tomorrow, in the Next 7 Days, and Later, as well as a calendar function for an overview (though the calendar somewhat lacks without the subscription), as well as a free pomodoro timer, an Eisenhower Matrix and a place to set and track habits. The widgets are a lifesaver, and customisable too, and can be changed to show anything from all of your tasks, one of your lists or today, the next 7 days or, with premium, a calendar with all your tasks blocked in. I have just subscribed to the premium version of the app after several weeks of use because the Eisenhower Matrix and calendar are really useful features that aren’t AS useful without the subscription, though still usable. Considering the low price and how brilliant this app has been, I just had to get the premium version, but believe me, it was great even without paying. Honestly, I could not ask more from an app!

title: Thought it was the best... until I reached the top 4-6%... then??? No!!!
body:
I’d been using TickTick for years & really thought it was the best out there... I shared it with my business partner and she agreed, we both felt increasingly motivated and it was great to see myself relentlessly climbing through the leaderboards... until I got in the top 4-6%, then, no matter how much I ramped up my use of the app... over a period of 4-6months the best I could do was watch myself gradually go down in the ratings. It became totally unworkable, it was literally a case of me using the app so much to try to keep moving against what appeared to be a relentlessly defeating tide... that it really started to impinge on my workload & I had to stop. Which is a shame because until then it was the best app out there, and I have yet to find another which I am as happy to work with.
Shame guys... just as you think, after two or three years, you are about to win the grand, super achiever prizes... the earth starts slipping away like mud beneath your feet and you’re spending waaaay too much time to even stay in one place. I hope they’ve fixed that up now... but otherwise, I’m looking elsewhere.

title: Great app with a massive flaw
body:
Really love this app in so many ways, great UI and the fact it is cross platform. However, there is one major issue that is a deal breaker for me. That is syncing, specifically background sync of the iOS app not working at all. As an example, if i create a task on my Mac or Apple Watch it does not appear on the phone app until the app is actually launched and manually refreshed. 

This is frustrating if I create a task on my Apple Watch, as the phone app is just not aware of the task until I actually go into the app and force it to refresh/sync. This means in some cases the phone app will not notify me of tasks (because it doesn’t even know they exist!).

This is a massive deal breaker, I mean one of the primary functions of this app is to notify of important tasks and it can’t always do that! It’s not just me either, search online and users have reported this issue multiple times over the years. The dev responds saying they are looking to improve the background automatic syncing but it’s still a problem. I was all ready to pay for the premium upgrade but now I’m unfortunately uninstalling the app. Such a shame.

I’m a Web Developer myself, and I really appreciate good UI/UX. This app has got it all. During my hands-on experience, every time I’ve thought of something I wanted to do (like create custom sections within my lists, for example) I’ve been able to do it.

It’s so perfectly designed that it’s inspired to write a review - and I rarely do. 

It even surprises me with insanely cool features like the ability to switch to a Kanban View to organise your workflow. This is just an absolute game changer for me!

Thanks so much for creating this app, guys! You’ve gained a super fan right here.

title: Amazing!
body:
When I saw YouTuber Marques Brownlee using this app I knew it’d have to have something going for it and wow! After two days it’s now replaced my whole calendar, notes and task management system. 

I’ve bought premium and introduced 3 others to the app. The simplicity of being able to schedule tasks and have them drop into the today view for checking off is amazing, which then repopulate the next day for a continuous workflow. It’s super helpful and useful for people with repeating daily tasks that need to be done at dynamic times on different days like myself. 

Once you’re ready to dive in you can also take it to the next level with multiple lists, groups, tags, urgency rankings and deadline dates to really get things organised and clean. The amount of functionality and complexity for such a simple app (on the outside) is great. 

The user interface and experience is also worth noting, you can tell that a lot of effort has gone into making everything clean and easy to use, theme options, dark modes, selectable app icons, custom quick actions, hide able buttons... all built for making the user experience excellent! Props to the dev team and everyone involved for building such a great app! 

Just try it out and find out for yourselves!

title: Best to-do app around
body:
I‘ve tried every task app around and found TickTick to be the best of the bunch.

It has all the basics like colour-coded lists, priority settings and tags, with a decent free tier unlike some other apps that make you pay just to get tags and notifications. 

Some of my favourite features are merge tasks (I use this to make my planned work tasks for the day into one checklist), saved templates and the percentage progress indicator which is automatic with subtasks but you can also drag it across manually on any task if you like.

And it has a few features that really should be standard in every task manager yet are almost always missing: calendar view, ability to view calendar events from multiple calendars, a proper notes section as well as comments, and proper subtasks in steps that don’t get added to your task count.

However the themes aren’t great - worst of all, dark mode is horrible as the text is all orange. There are lots of new colour options but loads of them look the same and frankly I preferred the old ones (I miss neon yellow). Markdown implementation is also really poor.

But it’s brilliant otherwise!

title: Best of the best
body:
I've tried so many task managers, literally all of them. 

All I can say is none of them offer as many polished features as ticktick. 

I can fault it. It has never crashed on me, the colour coding is beautiful, the ability to organise inside the app is unbeatable, there are smart lists, location based reminders, alarms which actually catch your attention and so many more flawless and polished features. 

Not to mention the web app, reliable syncing, and the ridiculously low price tag that comes with the pro version. 

Oh yeah, and subtasks too!! 

I used to use "Things", and got fed up with their slow progress. Fair enough, they "apparently" spend so long because they polish out all of their bugs, but I think that's a load of rubbish as Ticktick has a shed load more features and they are all flawless and perfectly functional. I genuinely don't know why ticktick isn't more popular than it is now, all I know is it should be leading the market.

So goodbye Things and hello Ticktick.

title: Best ToDo/Task Management app!!
body:

This is by far the best ToDo/Task Management app I've ever used, and, believe me, I've tried hordes of them! It gives me all the features I need to organize everything I do, and it's so easy to work with that it brings a whole new level of meaning to the term user-friendly. I specially love the customizable repeats, the sub-tasks feature, which lets me track all the details I want to see while still only taking up one line on my to-do list, and today's tasks showing up in my Notifications so I can see my upcoming tasks with just one swipe. This is the Task Manager that I've been looking for - can't recommend too strongly!

The app is perfectly designed for easily creating new tasks, adjusting due dates and categorizing or prioritizing tasks. I love the simplicity of the home task list screen and the amount of detail you can add within individual tasks. Other features such as the notification centre widget and reminders are also very useful. TickTick is absolutly ideal for me as a busy student and I strongly reccommend anyone giving it a go!

title: Great App, Minor updates
body:

Today the Daylight saving hours have started/ended for a lot of regions. My app didn’t update based on the system timing. There is no option to change it manually. Please try to resolve this asap. I almost missed a meeting due to the issue. It doesn’t work as expected and also it didn’t update the future tasks as well. This might a huge hit for people depending on the app for their entire routine. Hope to hear from the team soon!!

Update: There was a slight delay (a weeks delay) in the US timing and the European timing when the day-light savings changed. The app updated perfectly when both the location adapted to the daylight savings. (If needed you can consider this case; It’s a rare case that people miss out during testing). Apart from that I love the app and it’s a vital part of my life. Updating the review with 5 stars. Kudos to the team.

title: Good for Businesses
body:
I’ve tried countless to-do and task management apps, but TickTick stands out as the most complete and intuitive solution. It combines everything I need — to-dos, calendar integration, reminders, habit tracking, and even a built-in Pomodoro timer — all in one beautifully designed interface.

The smart lists, tags, and priority levels make organizing my day effortless. I especially love the seamless sync across devices and how it fits perfectly into my workflow. Whether it’s for work, personal goals, or team projects, TickTick has genuinely improved my productivity and focus.

Highly recommend it to anyone who wants to get things done without the clutter. Worth every bit of the premium plan too!

title: Magnifica ma si può far di meglio.
body: Possiede un sistema di organizzazione molto più strutturato e completo rispetto ai suoi competitor oltre che la migliore offerta di widget, per chi fosse interessato. Uniche pecche, le dipendenze (subtasks), che non arrivano a più di 5 livelli. Inoltre un task può essere condizione necessaria solo di uno. Alle dipendenze si aggiungono il problema del "task composto": i frammenti di cui è composto un task non sono programmabili come un normale task, puoi impostare solo il promemoria ma non la durata nel calendario. Sempre con i task composti, non è possibile scomporre in altri task più piccoli un frammento. Infine non la programmazione dei task: se il 2 febbraio io volessi programmare un compito da fare necessariamente entro il 17 febbraio, per esempio, e decidessi di farlo il 4 febbraio nel calendario, dovrei inserire il periodo entro cui è possibile fare il task e poi impostare un promemoria ma non inserire contemporaneamente "quando fare il task", il task ha come proprietà solo un periodo. Metto 5 stelle però perché tra tutte è la più usabile però per i progetti a lungo termine (almeno un mese) non è la "to-do" app migliore, sicuramente la più usufruibile.

title: Quasi perfetta
body:
La uso quotidianamente, é ottima.
 Alcune migliorie che suggerisco:

- quando si sceglie di avere una notifica il giorno prima dell’evento non viene specificato che il task è futuro e non immediato: non viene scritto “tomorrow: … “ ma direttamente la task. Gradirei che sia esplicitata meglio data e ora direttamente dalla notifica, cosi da non pensare di dover fare una cosa quando in realtà è programmata nei giorni successivi.

- Su ipad non si può trascinare files o foto da TickTick ad un’altra app (per esempio files, foto). 

- Le liste condivise non funzionano con rapidità: la task pubblicata da una persona appare dopo troppo tempo, anche ore. (Paragone fatto con app “promemoria” di IOS con lista condivisa)

- Non è possibile evitare che gli habit siano considerati al pari delle task: i badge notifica sull’app restano anche se un habit non ritengo sia (per suo significato) importante quanto una task.

title: La migliore
body: Questa applicazione è incredibile. L’ho scoperta per caso, e dopo aver provato TUTTE le To Do app posso dire di aver trovato la migliore. L’idea di chiudere i task sul calendario integrato ha fatto la differenza. Con altre app mi capitava di non terminare tutto, ed era frustrante dover spostare liste di task di giornata in giornata. Questo avveniva perché, non utilizzando il calendario, sovrastimavo ciò che mi era possibile fare in un giorno. Ma, ho scoperto, il calendario è indispensabile. Questa è anche la caratteristica principale di TickTick. Recentemente ha aggiunto la possibilità di tracciare le abitudini, addirittura di misurare il tempo dedicato a ciascun task attraverso il pomodoro timer integrato. Cosa chiedere di più? In un colpo solo ha sostituito tutte le app che utilizzavo in precedenza. Una delle poche app a meritare la sottoscrizione: offre continuamente valore e nuove funzionalità.

La consiglio soprattutto per la possibilità di incastrare nel calendario gli impegni messi nelle liste e soprattutto per la nuova funzione di far vedere il tempo passato in “focus” (pomodoro e stopwatch) sul calendario! Utilissima, così da vedere quanto tempo si è speso per fare cosa.
Non dimentichiamo i rumori ambientali presenti durante le sessioni di focus: i migliori, ce ne sono di tantissimi tipi e sono davvero super stimolanti. 
Consiglio l’abbonamento che è davvero un piccolissimo prezzo per sostenere tutte le funzioni e soprattutto per continuare a ricevere questi bellissimi aggiornamenti! Non smettete mai.

title: Ad oggi, la migliore per me

Ho trovato TickTick, e anche se non è perfetta quanto Things ci si avvicina molto. E’ multipiattaforma, elegante, efficace e ragionevolmente economica. Ad oggi, giugno 2019, non credo ci sia di meglio sul mercato.

E le ho provate TUTTE. Omnifocus, Things, Todoist, RTM, Microsoft Todo, 2Do, Wunderlist, Toodledo, Asana, e chi più ne ha più ne metta.

title: Habits QoL requests
body:
Thanks for updating the Habits feature, devs! Export feature is still welcome :)
_____

Long time TickTick user. I like the app, I love how cross platform it is and the addition of the Habits feature is great. I do have some Quality of Life requests for it: - Allow a user to reset a habit count. This is useful when adding new habits and wanting to start counting old and new habits all at once. Or if you just want to refresh your habit performance. - Besides "Current streak" and "Total days", add the "Best streak" statistic in the list view. It's nice to see all the breakable records at once. - Add a “% Completed” statistic. Or a “Total Habit Days” and “Total Days Completed” statistic, instead of just the "Total Days" statistic. You want to get a good sense of how much you're sticking to a certain habit and that can be hard to tell, since each habit can have a different schedule. - Add the possibility to export your habit performance. I can imagine you won’t be adding full fledged weekly, monthly and yearly habit reports and nice habit graphs to the app. I can create these things myself though, if you’d allow me to export the data. Thanks for considering!

title: Great app but locks in, not out
body:
It works great, best app for tasks management I’ve seen so far. Of course there are some functional wishes to fulfill and I really can’t figure out why tasks, notes and habits should be separate data items or areas within the app.

The main reason I gave it a one star rating is the lack of security. Come on, it’s 2021. Cybercrime is all over the place. And this app still doesn’t offer two-factor authentication to lock the bad people out. Not even as a premium feature. Besides that, when trying to export my data there are only some text based options and copy-paste actions. Feels like locking me in.

The day this is fixed I’ll reconsider my exit.

title: Best time management app I have ever used.
body:
I really like TickTick! 

Have been using it for a week now and I must say it completely lives up to my expectations. Coming from Google Keep and Google Calendar (which are not integrated and both look ugly), this management system is a breath of fresh air. Really enjoying it! I have bought Pro subscriptions for both myself and my girlfriend so we can create lists together, anytime, anywhere. I love the fact that we can add comments to checklists so we can discuss details without changing the list.

One feature that I'm still missing (and would be nice if this is added), is the ability to create more hierarchy. Especially for business purposes, sometimes I want to create sublists for various list items. Like in Microsoft Word: when creating a list you can press "Tab" and it will indent the list item. I wish TickTick would also have a feature like that. It would make my lists even more structured.

Thanks again for making this awesome application and please keep up the good work!

title: Fantastic, most inclusive app but a few improvements need to be made
body:
- The "total count" of habit completion is literally a total count of how many times you've completed the habit. It really needs to be a streak feature like nearly all other habit apps. 
- habits need the ability to add a description to them. 
- unlimited checks on habits would be great. For example, if you complete the habit more than what you've set it to in the app you can't record this
- sub habits would also be a cool feature
- you are unable to see past events from synced calendars. This is the most ridiculous downside of the app and I've never seen another app do this. 
- the mobile app is a bit confusing design wise. The iPad and Mac apps on the other hand are amazing. 
- "dark mode" support would be a real bonus

title: Going backwards - cannot currently recommend
body:
I am a very experienced and long-term GTD to-do app user and I have used almost all the platforms out there.

This is the second time I have updated this review and sadly I am downgrading my rating of this app substantially.

The TickTick folk seem to be overwhelmed with the app's success and unable to keep up. Their responsiveness to support enquiries has dropped off badly.

Worst of all, background sync has become a universal problem with the app - previously it was best-in-class. Numerous users complain of this and nothing has been done to address it for months now.

Compared to other to-do and GTD apps, functionality is fairly powerful and usability is pretty good, once you get used to its quirky approach.

Lack of sub-projects is a shame, with the checklist option per task only a partial solution. And a limited set of annoying reminder sounds is ... annoying!

I would love to recommend this app, but cannot until they sort out some fundamental problems, especially background sync between platforms.

Take the "templates" feature for example. It's neat until you realize it's incredibly tedious to bring up. Or "hidden time" on the calendar view defaulting to "on" everytime the app boots for the first time. A particular one I find frustrating is sometimes it wouldn't default to "today" and instead be on the past day when switching between calendar and task pages, resulting in me being incredibly confused and frazzled until I realized it wasn't today that I was viewing. title: Life changer
body:
Before using TickTick, I felt bored and insignificant. Listing your goals, being organized, listing your task and making good habits makes you feel occupied and happy.

Ticking off tasks and habits are satisfying. It makes you feel accomplished. It’s also nice to see your accomplished task wether big or small. It makes you feel that your life is going to a good direction.

It’s also fun to list ideas and bucket lists that you can do in the future. You often forget these things but TickTick makes it sure that every good ideas, videos, articles and thoughts can be saved in a neat, smart place.

TickTick is my virtual assistant, life manager, secondary brain and friend. If you want to change your life, TickTick can help you with that. Trick is to setup a habit in your app to ‘check TickTick daily’. I’ve been using it for two weeks now and I can say I’ve never been this productive.

I suggest going premium and take control of your life. Ideas are precious things and shouldn’t be flying somewhere. Who knows? Maybe your small ideas and habit can bring you thousands or maybe millions of money.

title: Gives you a productivity boost
body:
The app helps one to be organized. I felt at first as if it wasn’t that intuitive to use (e.g. couldn’t find the settings, where to set events, templates, etc.), but I couldn’t help but wonder what people are raving about in the reviews. So I tried to read about the different features and now I love it. I maintain 3 separate physical notebooks for different things, but all of them have been nicely captured and catered in the app now. 

Some of the many great features:
* Making a template. Very useful for lists that are constant. You can add the template as a to-do, but can also add some more items to the list (once it’s in the calendar) without affecting the template. 
* Creating sub-tasks. Very helpful for situations like grocery shopping. You don’t want a long list of to-dos filled only with grocery items. This groups the items so list looks much cleaner. 
* Folders and sub-folders. Keeps things organized. 
* Arrange Tasks feature. Lets you see overdue tasks and allows you to re-schedule them on your own and not just pile up in and clutter the next day. 

I haven’t dived into every feature yet, but I can see how helpful they are when I start really using them. 

Nice to have: 
* To show tasks as textboxes in the calendar month-view, to easily distinguish an event from a task. 
* Allow changing of color for the other iCloud categories so that it can match the color of the corresponding categories in TickTick. 
* Add events that can be categorized as one of the categories in TickTick. 

Thank you for this app! Hopefully we get a lifetime subscription plan.

I get to have a calendar, a habit tracker, to do list, pomodoro, and also a search function. It’s so generous, what else does this app offer that I don’t know yet?! 

The UI is a beauty. I myself is a very picky person when it comes to frontend design, but what you have is just perfectly done. I’m inlove. What I’d like to see in the future is to have more color options for the widgets or make the widget color similar to the theme/color selected in-app and make the text a little smaller for the Daily View widget. title: Perfect combination of features
body: I am not new to this — over the years, I tried to build an optimal GTD-style productivity system in: Evernote, Things, OmniFocus and Todoist (not to mention countless attempts at custom solutions). I always ended up missing some elements I needed. E.g. with Todoist — the calendar view was underbaked, and I had to use Session for focus and time tracking. With the heavy-weight OmniFocus, with all customization options, the note support was abysmal. I have never felt more at home then I do with this app. It complements GTD in delightful ways: having trouble doing your weekly reviews or cleaning your inbox? Use the habit tracker! Some really big deadlines looming, but mixing with less important ones? Use Countdown. There’s more — The Pomodoro implementation  beats Session single - handedly in seamless integration with your task manager, while Session itself is almost twice the monthly price? The calendar is flexible, integrates without missing a beat, and is actually useful. Notes are fully realized, and can be used as a major part of the workflow. The API is quite flexible, if you want to ” roll your own” based on TickTick. The app works great on Mac, iPad, and iPhone. My only wish is custom dark themes — it was unexpected that customization applies to light themes only. The 1 dark theme is quite good though. Importantly, the app seems to click quite well with my ADHD too. Overall, cancelled my monthly subscriptions and went to annual within a week.

Oh god TickTick is SOOO much better, to be fair though I’m unsure how much of that is “objective” vs just my specific brain liking the aesthetic, the design, the features and just about damn near everything about this app but yeah I personally LOVE this app.

title: Amazing app, but lacking in some areas
body:
I have used TickTick for about a year now. It is absolutely one of the best ToDo-apps I have used (and I have used a lot!). 
But it’s lacking in three areas: 

1. Gamification. It has some badges but they are not very motivating and not very visible or integrated. I would really like more levels, and more “rewards” for the levels (maybe a new theme unlocking for example? I would also like to have different tasks weighted differently. If there is a task I have procrastinated for month, I would like to gather more points for completing it. 

2. “Nudging” feautures. I wish TickTick would take inspiration from Amazing Marvin which is superb in this area. They have feautures such as “task jar”, “random task”, “beat the clock”, “super focus mode”, “procrastination wizard” etc. 

3. Personalisation. Even though TickTick is already better in this area than many other apps in the same category, there is still A LOT of room for improvement. Again, I wish TickTick would learn from Amazing Marvin here. 

If these three areas were optimised, I would give TickTick a solid 10 out of 5!

title: Exceptional Work!
body:
Honestly, TickTick stands shoulder to shoulder with the best productivity apps out there. It handles continuity, syncing, and day to day task management extremely well. As a core to-do list manager, it really shines.

But no app nails every single category, and TickTick has a couple spots where it could level up. The Pomodoro feature is the main one. It doesn’t really need its own bottom tab just to show a single “Start” button. That space could be used for something more functional. The timer would make more sense sitting inside the “Home” tab, right next to your tasks, so it naturally supports the list you’re actually working on. A Pomodoro should feel integrated, not separate.

The Habit Tracker could also benefit from duration tracking. If I plan to read for 15 minutes but end up reading for 25 minutes, that extra effort should be reflected. And yes, there’s the Pomodoro timer, but it doesn’t fully connect to either habits or tasks, so the ecosystem never quite syncs together the way you’d hope.

And clearing out bad habits could definitely be more intuitive and front and center.

All that said, TickTick is still an excellent app. For what it offers, it provides exceptional value, and the overall experience is hard to beat. With a few thoughtful adjustments, it could easily become the gold standard for productivity apps.

title: My favorite and only Todo list app.
body: I had been falling behind on my todos and today thought it would be a good idea to just print them out to keep them in mind… and even the printout is so well designed, with clear to read formatting, and organization… it made me remember how thankful I am for this tool. I started using TickTick more than a couple of years ago having outgrown other todo trackers, and have never had to look again. What I like about it? It is so well designed, so many todo apps do not seem to have had a designer involved in the process, but whoever designed TickTick fully understood how to make an intuitive, clear to read, engaging interface. I love the organization of folders tasks and sublists and that you can tag your todos, ooh the power of tagging goes unrealized by so many apps (notability hint hint). I use TickTick to organize and track my small business, my household and my family todos. The pricing, free, is amazing without any obtrusive ads. And I am also here to upgrade, which is so reasonable, compared to the math apps that I use which unreasonably expect me to pay $10 a month each —TickTick is in the $2 range for additional forward looking functionality. Thank you TicktTick for keeping me organized. I might not always get to everything that I put in there, but that feeling that you got my back motivates me to keep moving forward.

title: EXACTLY WHAT I NEEDED!!
body: So I’ve waited quite some time before I wrote a review just so that I had enough time to use every aspect of the platform in both the free and the pro version and then got comfortable enough with it to utilize it on my day-to-day. Honestly, the aesthetics of it are great. I love that you can toggle between light and dark mode. It’s got really useful widgets and all features are incredibly customizable as well, which is another big plus. It’s super simple if I wanna add a quick task to my day or an event to my calendar. And it’s equally as quick if I want to check off an item after completion. I love that it keeps track of my daily habits and how it gamifies them so it definitely makes my to-do list feel a lot more doable. It even has a Pomodoro timer, there’s a countdown feature and even an Eisenhower matrix. It’s super simple but incredibly loaded down with all the good stuff so I think it’s the perfect blend of what you would expect something like this to have and what you really would love for it too include. I use it every single day and I really like it. It is become my go to for schedule keeping and I was someone who used to toggle between the Things App, Sorted and Fantastical lol. Kudos to the creators because they not only hit the mark on usability and features, but they also do their part with maintenance and upkeep always adding new things and doing updates so if you do download this app, do yourself a favor and just splurge that little bit on the pro version you will not regret it and it’s so affordable to boot!

title: Fantastic To DoApp. great for GTD
body:
I’m a to do list junkie and have tried almost all the other tools. I find TickTick to be the best fit for me. I follow the GTD methodology and this tool makes it easy. I appreciate how I can use it on virtually any device, including my iWatch. The iWatch integration is fantastic because I can quickly add reminders any time by pressing one button and speaking the task. I did not initially realize how useful this feature is. For example, I often want to create reminders while driving or walking the dog.
In addition, there is excellent calendar integration, custom smart views, sorting, sharing, tags, locations, habits, summary reporting, file attachments, timers, integration with Spark email and Amazon Alexa, and focus mode with soothing sounds and a Kanban view on some platforms.
I’m impressed with this tool and highly recommend it. You can try many of the functions for free to see if this tool works for you. I believe the price is low considering the excellent functionality and product quality. I like the subscription model since it motivates the developers to continue enhancing their product. 
Please note this is my personal opinion. I have no relation to the developers or their company, and I paid for the product subscription with my own personal funds.

title: I want you to fix this.
body:
This is an amazing app, and I use it every day. However, there’s one thing I’d really like to see improved.

When I want to type something like “1-4pm” in the title of an event, the app automatically interprets it as a date and time.

For example, if I enter:
“1-4pm rehearsal”

the app treats “1-4” as January 4, and “4pm” is removed from the title and used as the event time instead.

I don’t want the app to interpret what I type—I just want the text to stay exactly as I entered it. Later, when I look for the event, I end up thinking, “I could have sworn I created it,” because it was changed automatically.

The automatic date and time recognition can be useful, but I’d really appreciate having an option to turn it off, or at least keep the text exactly as typed instead of modifying it automatically.

title: ♥️ Love this App - Helps with ADHD. (Some Suggestions)
body:
Feedback:
- Please add the ability to save different filters for views on the calendar & Eisenhower, rather than having to manually switch
- Please make it so we can have multiple Eisenhower Matrices

Honestly love this app. Syncs with my Google tasks and calendar. I was able to do a two way sync with tasks by using Zapier. It allows me to continue to use my AI for calendar & task management 😃.

Eisenhower & priority views are tremendously helpful for me as my ADHD forgets to prioritize properly. I usually end up not prioritizing properly. Having both of the views helps tremendously when planning my day.

LOVE the widgets. I have a focus mode and shortcut on my iPad that immediately takes me to my ‘planner’ page, consisting of the many widgets available for use. I love this and it is so incredibly helpful for my ADHD to be able to see everything at once.

I am incredibly grateful to the creators of this app, you guys definitely deserve all the positive comments! 

The pomodoro timer in the app allows you to choose the task, time and has a pop-out timer. On behalf of ADHD folks, thank you! 😭⚡️

On a side note, having different calendar views saved for filtering could help in cases of families sharing accounts. I share a calendar with my BF and because my view for my daily tasks heavily relies on prioritizing, the lack of color for mine vs boyfriends calendar events can be a bit confusing.

title: Most helpful
body:
As an older man who has suffered with ADHD most of my life, I am always searching for a program or app to help me get my mind organized. Ticktick is the first one that has helped. It allows me to do a brain dump from my mind into a list in the app. I can then put a date, priority, recurring, etc., and keep track of them all on a calendar.  That way I’m looking at tasks to do gradually instead of just looking at one giant list and getting overwhelmed.Best of all, it syncs everywhere, so I never have to wait to add a task. I even have it on my Windows desktop.

Tick tick has been a lifesaver. Now, instead of looking at paper lists everywhere, I can quickly add a task to a list and schedule it. I even have a separate list for household items where I keep track of bills to pay. There has been a bit of a learning curve (an online manual would be great.) but once you learn it, you find how easy it is to use. There’s so many other things that this program does; I can’t recommend it enough.

title: Fantastic except for one confusing problem…
body:
More user friendly than Todoist- also looks better because of recent updates. I think it is the best to do list all that exists. Full stop. And I’ve tried way too many.

The only problem it has: I use the date property in my tasks to mark their deadlines, if they have deadlines- when they’ve got to be done by. I usually try to complete those tasks long before the deadline comes. How should I use the calendar feature in TickTick to schedule my tasks with time blocking? If I put them on my calendar for when I will do them, then the date property no longer represents the deadline for the task. So, I simply can’t use the calendar for time blocking. Isn’t that supposed to be the main purpose of having a calendar inside TickTick? Unfortunate. 

Adding a separate date property called “deadline“ would be awesome. For most people, only a small portion of their tasks would have true deadlines. The current date property could be used to indicate when the user plans to complete the task. The new “deadline” property would represent when they need to complete it by, at the latest. To be able to filter tasks to see only ones with deadlines would be great.  To sort by deadline would be great too. Then you could reschedule your tasks in the calendar using the primary date property while still being able to keep track of their deadlines. 

Users could also view both when they plan to complete the task as well as when the task is due on the calendar. Those two dates would need to be visually differentiated of course, so users could tell them apart.

Some casual users might never understand the purpose of the extra “deadline” property, and that’s totally fine.

If this was done, TickTick would be a near perfect app.

Every "X" days feature is actually so underrated—not one app really nails that like TickTick. Apple doesn't ship with that in its reminders app; Microsoft doesn't either; Samsung, same thing, I presume… You get what I mean. I can select something like every 3 days and I'm not forced to pick out specific weekdays (although that is an option), I can actually just select every 3 days as I should be.

I use this to sort out my dosing regarding my supplement stack. This app helps to keep me healthy and does the hard part for me every time: remembering. This is so perfect.

title: Simple, Effective and helps me Get things done
body:
I can go ahead and compare the app with other To-Do apps I have used earlier. But, I think what makes Tick Tick a great app is not the to do part but the additional layers built on top of the classic To-Do list. Some of my favorites were:
1. Eisenhower matrix: might look trivial until we try it. Extremely helpful when you are juggling a lot of tasks.

title: this app is one of the best things in my life and i literally evangelize it to anyone and everyone
body:
i’ve been using tick tick for a few years now. important background info: i LOVE planning, i love categorizing, i love organization, i love note keeping and collecting and compiling information and media of all kinds. i love being able to customize and design any system i interact with to my needs and preferences as much possible. (i am an engineer and also autistic so when i say i love this stuff, i mean it. it’s a genuine passion and hobby for me) 

ticktick is fantastic for so many reasons, the fact that it’s cross platform is already just a huge huge plus. but i think ticktick’s design philosophy is what makes it so great. there are so SO many features, there are so many way to customize things, there are so many ways to tailor your tick tick exactly to your needs. if you want simplicity, you don’t have to deal with using extra complex features that you don’t need, especially since oftentimes complex or intricate functions and options are actually a hindrance for those who don’t need it. 

with tick tick, you can make your lists, notes, whatever, as simple as you want. you don’t need to deal with unnecessary complications if you don’t want them. nor do you have to deal with the visual clutter of features you don’t even use. this is a common issue i find on program and app design, where the excessive amount of options and buttons and features make them difficult to navigate and ultimately i will stop using them. and i love that tick tick puts so much work and effort into providing a wealth of options for customization ad well as options to interlink various notes, tags, media, you name it. but they also understand that is not what everyone needs, and they make it so so accessible and easy to just make simple lists without extra hassle or having some useless premium feature shoved in your face every time you open the app. 

for someone like me, i use basically all of the functions and features, i have created a wiki of sorts for various notes, i even use the link feature to link to notes in my native notes app! i love that you can create note folders/lists. its perfect for me as I can keep EVERYTHING i need in one place. 

i have a list that’s just full of resources and user guides for my electronics/tools and other things i reference a lot. it’s so amszingly helpful. I have a note list that contains helpful keyboard shortcut cheat sheets for various apps, and tick ticks sticky note feature allows me to pin those to the screen when i need them! i have a note list for shopping and wishlists, projects i want to do in the future.

i even have a list of notes ABOUT tick tick (because i am not normal about this obviously lol) including an in progress visual user guide im working on for my friends because i want to convert them, a note of various features i think would be great additions, user feedback, a list of things to add to my tick tick. 

i could give so many more examples of the amazing ways you can use this app to make it perfect for what you need, but i genuinely doubt anyone is still reading this far haha. 

as i said at the bringing of this novel of a review, lists and organizing and planning is a hobby and passion to me. if i get to spend a weekend entirely making and arrange lists, information, and spend time and energy to do it efficiently, affectively, accessibly, with optimized and streamlined design and of course above all, approachable, usable, easy to understand, and something that i can actually keep up with. balancing simplicity and readability with my love for automation, detailed descriptions and breakdowns of tasks, as well as notes and information i find relevant. i will be on cloud nine having the time of my life and then show off my work to my lowed ones who are very patient with me haha. 

so you can TRUST ME when I say this is an AMAZING app, i love it, and i know what im talking about ;p it’s the best one ive used and trust me i have used a lot lol. 

i will say that tick tick seems to be optimized and made for primarily people using it on their phone (which makes sense, it’s an app haha) and while the cross platform ability is so helpful, i find that the desktop version of the app (specifically the mac version) doesn’t receive updates as frequently, and i believe is missing features that are available on the phone app. 

also, the aesthetic customization on the desktop is both tedious and difficult to use for custom backgrounds, as the ability to preview and estimate the photo sizes to use and how they will actually look when applied makes it a long process for me. additionally (last i checked) the mac version doesn’t have the font customization features available
on windows :( it also doesn’t allow you to alter the text/font of “pinned” lists/folders. meaning that if the title of the pinned note is too long, it just gets cut off. i would even just like the ability to turn off the title text beneath the pins and just use the emojis for them so i don’t have to deal with the cut off titles. 

it would also be great to have a little more freedom in the custom theme options like picking your accent color and maybe some control over the actual text in the app, as it’s difficult to use a custom image and find a balance of opacity/blur/brightness that will make the text readable. which often means the photo you wanted as your background has to be very purposely sized and strategically placed, and usually ends up being far more cut off or distored/blurred than what you wanted in order to accommodate text visibility, since as i recall, you don’t get to pick the color of the text or like if it’s light mode/dark mode or whatever. 

all that being said, i am very neurotic and also love making things cute so im pretty sure no other person would care about all that. 

anyways perfect app, and if you’ve read all the way to the end of this, genuinely thank you lmao

title: Great Platform - Annoying App
body:
Everything i Love about TickTick on the web I HATE about the app.

I love that it took 15 minutes to learn the tool, and the relief was immediate. 

I love that it’s not bloated with design and integration features and options. 

The App? The opposite.

To check off yesterday’s habit i have to: click on the habit, slide up to the calendar view, click on the day, THEN click on the checkmark - not the smiley face, then return to the calendar screen, and exit out if that to get back to habits view.

WHY??!?!

All i need is an ON/OFF toggle on the calendar. Thats all. Editable. I never did figure out how to uncheck a day on my phone. 

It got so annoying I opted to leave this review on my commute rather than keep going.

Clean it up!! 

People who love TickTick are efficient minimalists. Maximalists and youngsters are using Notion, Obsidian and all that other stuff. I left Todoist because there were too many unnecessary buttons and features for me. 

Let Tick Tick be what its best at: small ticks - BIG difference.
Thanks.

body:

title: Great app
body: I’ve been using TickTick for a couple of years now and definitely feel the price point for value is worth it. I primarily use this in my job to manage tasks and projects. The best way I can put it - is it’s pretty customizable with different setups/views - try it out and explore. How I set up and organize things may not be how someone else would and TickTick accommodates both. I will say - the web browser is nice to setup your whole layout and explore - I use the phone app to input things quickly and reference mostly. Features I love: being able to print things out, constant reminders until you complete a task, attaching document files to tasks (word,excel,PDFs…) that one is huge. There’s more I encourage you to explore. They keep this price point to value ratio and I’ll be a customer for a long long time.

title: Amazing task app!
body: Before downloading TickTick, I really struggled finding a task app with all the features I wanted. Things like due dates, reminders prior to due dates, calendar view, etc. I was totally excited to download TickTick and see that they have all of those capabilities and more! I group up each task by list, and with a life that consists of work tasks, home tasks, social tasks, and misc tasks... I LOVE the organization and it is much needed! The reminders are easy to receive and creating a task is so easy. Sometimes I’ll create a task whenever I’m thinking about it and that weight can be lifted off my shoulders because I know TickTick will remind me when I actually need to think about that task, but when it gets closer to time I panic thinking I forgot something until I look at the calendar view and see it was there all along! I pay for the premium version ($2.99 a month I believe) because it’s totally worth it to get to change themes and do other things like change the duration of how long a task will take. All in all, TickTick is my favorite and most used app on my phone! The only thing I wish that was a little smoother was adding a location to a task, such as an address... I’d like to be able to just click on the address and it take me to my Maps app but usually I have to copy and paste. Very tiny detail though :) great job making an app for your users, TickTick!

title: So much potential
body:
I wanted to like TickTick because the layout and features look great, but the calendar/task distinction is incredibly confusing and poorly explained.

Creating a recurring appointment (like weekly therapy) should be straightforward, but depending on how you create it, the same item can randomly behave like a task, an event, or both. Converting a task to an event breaks recurring calendar visibility, and there’s no clear indication of what type something actually is.

As a free user, day/week views are locked, which makes it even harder to understand why some items show on the calendar and others don’t. I spent way too long troubleshooting something that should take 30 seconds.

The app needs a clear, visible distinction between tasks and calendar events, or at least better guidance

title: All style and little substance. Glaring interface gaps make this not worth the price
body: Have been using for about half a year now and while there is a lot to like, the seemingly obvious gaps in interface options are irritating enough to have me looking elsewhere. The inability to choose what time intervals you want your constant reminder in (and the fact that they are not constant) seems almost …insane considering what the point of the app is, if your task can’t be completed in 5 minutes with a very loud alarm going off every 30 seconds good luck. Being able to have an hourly reminder for tasks that may take the whole day feels so obvious and yet they’ve chosen to not offer that despite their user’s requests. Not being able to organize my daily list by newest to oldest… i mean… just why?? Why would i not be able to do that? It feels like they’ve made their product and have zero interest in making sure it is able to help with any kind of diverse task management. Oh also if you have multiple tasks with reminders set at the same time your push notification will just say “3 tasks” instead of what they are… and no option to change that, what gives? All style and no substance sums up my experience with this app

title: great for planning with adhd

My biggest struggles with my adhd is my planning, time management, and prioritizing tasks, and it's awesome I get to do all that from here. I still need to figure out the pomodoro and habit tracking features, but I'm sure those will help as well down the line. I also like it's not trying to push some ai bot that's gonna schedule everything for me. I just needed a spot to dump my thoughts and organize from there. Having a huge widget that shows my list without me having to open the app also helps. I'm terrible with "out of sight out of mind" kind of stuff, so it's a better way to remind someone like me who might not immediately remember if I don't have a notification on. Plus the planner looks cute with the little theme I gave it. So far, 10/10.

title: Amazing productivity and task managing app
body:
This is quite simply one of the absolute best to do list and overall productivity apps I have ever used in my 16 years as an iPhone user.

First and foremost, it allows you to pick which functions you need and which you don’t: calendar, Eisenhower matrix, habit tracker, pomodoro timer, etc.

Then, the Eisenhower matrix function alone is more powerful and allows for more color-coding, categorization and reminder settings – even in just the free tier – than some dedicated matrix apps (i.e. Focus Matrix, Priority Matrix).

The habit tracker function alone is essentially the entire “Productive - Habit Tracker” (app as it was in 2017) crammed into a single tab on this app.

I am impressed and blown away and plan to continue using this app many years into the future, even despite already having and using Focus Bean, Proton Calendar, outset, and of course, the basic iOS apps. 

Here’s to many more years of insanely powerful and thorough project/habit/task tracking & management.

title: Tick Tick over Todoist
body:
Writing a review because another reviewer knocked off two stars because there aren’t enough free themes! This is after gushing how much the app improved their life. Really? Thanks for making my life better, but you’re not giving me enough for free!

Tick Tick has the most robust free version of any to do app, hands down. If need more themes, maybe you should pay.

If you’re new to the to do app game, you’ve come to the right place. It’s Tick Tick or Todoist. Like many, I prefer Todoist’s interface, but Tick Tick has features I’m not willing to give up. Todoist has a cleaner interface because it has fewer features and is less customizable, so there it is. 

For me it’s the Widgets and the ability to use Tick  Tick as a second brain.  

Tick Tick also costs less last time I checked.

Often my life is full of post it’s and to do lists everywhere. I have tried so many apps and it works for a while but after a while does not seem to fit my needs. This has reduced my stress dramatically because I can easily capture thoughts with one click. I am a morning person and often on my way to work I have all these ideas pop into my head that I want to capture. With this I literally start talking and it puts it directly into my “inbox”. Boom out of my brain and I can mentally move forward. This is just one of the gazillion ways I use this app. The best app I have ever used. Much love to the person that created this app - thank you. ❤️

title: Best Personal Tasking App
body:
I’ve been a paid super user for 4+ years now. Honestly it’s a game changer. I don’t think I could live without this or an app like this. It’s simple enough to just start with and once it becomes a habit to always come to the app whenever a new thing pops up in your head, it’s like a brain massage to reduce anxiety and create momentum.

With this said, I’d love a feature of a kanban view to track tasks differently than “incomplete or complete”

Sometimes I will push off a task because there’s other things I am waiting on (from team for example), and I want to be able to highlight those as a separate tag in a kanban view. Things like “In progress, Blocked, Waiting on Somrthing, etc…”

Clickup has a similar feature but it’s designed for teams so from a personalization standpoint this takes the cake. Try the app out if you haven’t, give it a solid week of energy, and your life will change.

title: Calendar App King
body:
I dont leave reviews..ever, but

The fact that TickTick not only did both but did them the right way, seamless, engaging, modern, not cluttered, and more amazes me. The only thing that actually ticks me is that I didn’t find out about this sooner. 

I have ADHD and an organization tool, this one specifically is one of, if not the most handy tool to help me navigate life. It keeps you accountable and engaged with the habit tracker heat map which is a big win.

I genuinely applaud and appreciate the work that was put into this app and hope it never goes away and that the developers dont try to go over their feet trying to achieve too much. You guys have something amazing here, please dont mess it up.

Thanks again to whoever built this.

title: Everything I ever needed
body: TickTick is an amazing productivity app if you can spare the 3 dollar/month premium fee. It allows you to easily track tasks in organized lists with task durations, due dates, and sub tasks. Tasks with due dates are connected to the calendar which make things extremely convenient and helps you see your day/week/month at a glance. There is a pomodoro/focus feature where you can log focused work hours and you can see your past durations - meaning if you have been focusing for one hour in previous seasions, you can try aiming for 90 mins. You get full control and customization over how you want to view tasks - you can view task lists by a certain category or time period, or you can view them in an Eisenhower matrix.

title: Need more artists work
body:
I really enjoy using this app — it’s smooth, useful, and well-designed. I do have a few suggestions that I think could make it even better:
	1.	Add More Fun Visuals: It would be awesome to have more playful or creative features, like uploading our own emojis or using fun reactions. It adds personality and engagement!
	2.	Organize Tasks by Categories/Files: I’d love a way to group tasks by themes or goals — like separate folders for work, study, travel, etc., each with different color codes (similar to Apple Calendar). Maybe this exists already, but I didn’t notice it.
	3.	Include a Habit Tracker + Insights: Adding a basic habit tracker would make the app feel more holistic — great for managing both tasks and personal growth. A simple stat dashboard showing completed tasks, overdue ones, and trends over time would be a helpful bonus. It would give users insight into their productivity and behavior.

Overall, this app is great — and with these improvements, it could easily become a one-stop productivity hub!

title: All the features, easy to navigate, easy to integrate with google calendar.
body:
I have used many productivity apps. I had settled into using each for the feature I liked best. Due for persistent reminders, Todoist for long-term projects like shopping lists, Habitica for habits and daily routines. 

TickTick handles almost all of these for me now. There’s nothing wrong with these other apps, but the way TickTick presents its various views works very well with my brain. As CGP Grey and Mike Hurley say on Cortex (paraphrased): “There are a million productivity apps because every person’s needs are slightly different.” Omnifocus provides all the features TickTick does, but my brain doesn’t navigate it easily like it does TickTick so I’ve never been able to fully utilize it. 

So what makes TickTick work for me? One would be the easy way you can change different projects to be a list, a kanban, or a timeline. The integration of natural language for setting dates is also excellent, but in particularly the advanced filters really let it shine. 

For example I wanted to have a list of day/night routine tasks that repeats daily. While I could have used the Habit system TickTick has (which may actually work better than my solution) I didn’t have time to learn it and wanted just a repeating daily checklist. 

I was able to make this checklist of repeating tasks, sorted into day/night categories via a kanban chart, THEN use a smart filter to create a view that hid them so they didn’t clog up my view of my other tasks due that day. 

Was this the optimal solution? Probably not. I may switch everything over to their habit tracker instead. However the flexibility of the app allowed me to build a system that works FOR ME instead of having to adapt to the app designers intended use case. That sort of flexibility is crucial for making systems that function and keep me organized even when I’m extremely busy. I was able to use knowledge I already had about the app (making lists, tagging, making filters) to build a routine system that works for me all in the short breaks during my work day. All with minimal googling. 

In short if you use multiple apps for a feature you like from them, try TickTick for a few days and see if it can merge some of those. I didn’t even mention that the widgets  work great for displaying specific filters or even an Eisenhower matrix, or the fact that it integrates BOTH WAYS with google calendar. I can’t overstate how nice it was to learn I can both intake events shared with me AND send my own to my google calendar. 

Honestly the worst thing about this app is the name (so annoying to search and explain to people with TikTok on the scene haha) and the appearance customization. I really wish the list colors were more than a thin left border, and that I was able to freely change the accent color of the dark mode. But these are minor gripes for an app that is so functionally sound.

title: Missing just one thing
body:
Hi, I wanted to say that I really love this app—it works great and has a lot of potential. I was planning to subscribe and continue using it, but there’s one key feature that’s holding me back: the inability to check off or mark recurring tasks as completed.

I have a list of daily tasks and really appreciate how they automatically show up each day. However, not being able to mark them as done takes away a big part of what makes task management effective—especially for someone like me with ADHD. Being able to check off a completed task provides a small but powerful dopamine boost that helps me stay motivated and consistent.

I truly hope this is something that will be added in the future. Until then, I’ll have to use an app that allows me to mark off recurring tasks, but I’d love to come back if this feature becomes available.

Thanks for all your hard work!

title: Great out of all the apps I’ve tried!
body: I’ve been using TickTick for 4 years now and I’ve recommended it to all my friends, family, and classmates. I really love the organization and structure of the app. I also appreciate the widgets for Apple and Android. There are a couple of things I wish the app could improve on. For example, I wish the colors I assign to certain folders were more prominent in different areas of the app. I also wish there was an option to create alarms (I love how you can sent reminders to repeat on every other Monday, third Thursday of the month, etc) I just wish there was the option to set the reminder as an alarm with customizable sounds or vibrations. Recently TickTick and Notion integrated (I’ve used notion before and it’s great!) I just hate how you have to pay. While TickTick is able to somewhat integrate into local calendars, I wish it was more integrated into other apps or aspects of my phone. If TickTick were to create reminders based on a class calendar or syllabus that would be awesome! Or if it could be connected to my Black Board calendar and import assignment due dates from there. One of my other critiques is the paywall behind certain features. When I first used the app, I had no problem with this. However, they put the constant reminder as a pro feature. This was really upsetting because one of the reasons I started using TickTick was because it was free. The paywalls don’t make the app unusable but I feel like the pro features aren’t worth paying so much money! Besides its drawbacks, TickTick has been amazing for keeping my school work and personal tasks under control. I sincerely recommend giving this app a try!!

title: Fantastic To Do List and Calendar Capabilities
body:
I got this app because I was looking for a great To-Do list app, one that I could break down my projects into tasks, in a way that made the most sense to me. 

While other To-Do list apps offer their unique features to help you keep track of your daily life, I kept coming back to TickTick because of the freedom it allows me to optimize whatever flow works best for me.  

I’ve been using premium for a year, and in that time I’ve completed more projects using TickTick than any other To-Do list app thus far.  

I think the best part is that it’s helped me start using a calendar in my life as well.  Before I would have had to use apple reminders app alongside the calendar app (which I never used the calendar app).  With the calendar integration, I’ve started using calendars in my life too, which has been nothing but helpful.

If I had to suggest anything for the TickTick team, I would like to see a way for users be able to “Draft” up new Folders, Tags, and Lists, so we can test new workflows before overhauling our current setups.  

With all the AI that’s available, I’ve been using it to help optimize my TickTick Folders, Tags, and Lists.  

I think some sort of “drafting” feature, which would allow us to test out new folders, lists, and tags, before actually moving/tagging our current workflow, could be a brilliant time saver.

Great app. Thank you.

title: Best Productivity App!
body:
As someone who has tried countless productivity apps, TickTick stands out as a true game-changer in personal organization. What sets it apart is its seamless integration of three essential productivity tools: a robust calendar view, an intuitive todo list, and a built-in Pomodoro timer - all working harmoniously in one unified interface.

The calendar integration is particularly impressive, offering a comprehensive overview of both your scheduled events and tasks. Being able to visualize your todo items directly within the calendar view helps tremendously with time blocking and realistic planning. The way tasks seamlessly sync with the calendar makes it feel like having a personal assistant who understands exactly how you want to organize your day.

What truly elevates TickTick is its integrated Pomodoro timer feature, which transforms task management from simple list-making into actual time-boxed productivity sessions. Having your focused work sessions visually represented in your calendar provides invaluable insights into how you're actually spending your time.

The synergy between these features creates an effortless workflow that helps you stay on top of your commitments while maintaining a healthy work rhythm. It's rare to find an app that so elegantly combines these essential productivity tools without feeling cluttered or overwhelming.

After experiencing how well these features work together, I can't imagine going back to using separate apps for my calendar, tasks, and time tracking. TickTick has become my go-to productivity hub, streamlining my daily planning and execution into one thoughtfully designed package. For anyone seeking a comprehensive productivity solution that brings together calendar management, task organization, and focused work sessions, TickTick is quite simply the best tool available.

title: Switched from Microsoft ToDo
body: As an avid Microsoft productivity app user, I wanted to love their ToDo app, especially since I already owned it. However, it lacked some important features — it would reset the “My Day” view every day at midnight, causing me to have to try to rebuild my tasks for the day in a flurry first thing in the morning. No one wants to start the day with anxiety. With some research, I found TickTick. Now I set my “Today” view every evening at the end of the workday so I wake up stress-free. I pin the tasks to get done first to the top of the day, set priorities, which shows them accordingly in the Einstein view, and when I open the app during my “coffee time,” there it all is, laid out perfectly so I can get right to being productive — no anxiety, no wondering if I forgot anything, the perfect task and ADHD time management tool. And well worth the ~$35/year. I haven’t tapped into all the features yet, like creating templates, setting up filters, and using the timeline view, but after using for only a few days so far, I’ve been amazed how easy it is to get up and running, and I’m looking forward to learning more.

title: The best thing that has ever happened to me

As someone with severe ADHD, executive functioning has always been a major struggle for me, making it difficult to get things done. title: TickTick gets the job done. Or, at least it helps me get the job done.
body: TickTick is a very basic task manager that offers as much complexity as most of us would want/need. Its list, calendar, and Eisenhower Matrix offer up multiple methods of managing tasks and projects. Throw in a Pomodoro to help with focus and your productivity can reach levels you haven’t known before. Additionally, TickTick offers task lists, powerful filtering, and an intuitive tag process to help manage personal and professional tasks. The reminder component can suit most any need to keep you on top of upcoming tasks individually and within projects. I almost forgot the multiple view modes for tasks. List view, kanban, and timeline offer up differing modes of presenting tasks based upon your needs. While we’re at it, let’s throw in a habit tracker that provides detailed statistics and feedback to assist you in developing habits. All-in-all, features to dollars spent, you’d be hard-pressed to find another manager that offers what TickTick does.
author: GTinKY

title: *THE ONLY* app for procrastinators and ADHD
body:
I have written 2 reviews in my entire life that I can remember and this is one of them.  I have been using the native Apple apps for years but I felt like they were always missing something. TickTick checked off those boxes it was missing (only thing I miss is Siri to take down reminders by voice, but I can live without).

For anyone with ADHD it is sometimes difficult to describe what is going on in your brain.  But this app is a literal screen shot of how my brain operates, especially the 4 quadrant priority check list.  The different calendar views and the quadrant is worth the sub alone. You can “zoom” as far out of your schedule as you want and you can “zoom” in as close as you want so you literally can visualize your schedule on a grand scale or a micro scale.  I tried other apps in conjunction with this one but in the first hour I knew this was it.  Give it a shot, if your brain is like mine, you’ll fall in love.

title: Near perfect but simple things could make it better

It helps keep people who are more externally motivated to stay on top of things and feel good about it.

When you check off tasks it should itself be rewarding. Like an animation and sound. When you finish a day or check off you last task some rewarding congratulations prompt would be nice. Heck even if they made stickers or some in app rewards would be cool. See things you unlocked after completing a day of tasks. 

Genuinely to me those things would be game changer. Making your own life feel like a bit of a game would be nice, motivating, and make the app like 2x better than the perfect app it already is. Really would love to just see it be a little above and beyond it has the potential.

title: Great for keeping everything organized!
body:
This app is one of the best reminder apps I've ever used. Each task can be set at a duration so it shows up in the calendar like an event, but can be checked off like an actual to-do list.

Separating things into folders provides further customization and organization; I use a "daily tasks/weekly tasks/monthly tasks/yearly tasks" approach, and within each folder, I can set up columns for categories. 

From tags to recurring tasks and subtasks, this app can do it all! I used to use Apple Reminders, but the subtasks on recurring tasks would stay checked (and therefore hidden) when completing them. That’s not a problem with TickTick; subtasks and recurring tasks work perfectly!

The Eisenhower Matrix helps prioritize my most important tasks alongside my currently due tasks. Plus, as someone with ADHD, the habit tracker for things like cleaning up, doing laundry, drinking water, exercising, and more custom habits make this app my one-stop-shop for ALL my reminders. 

I can’t recommend this app enough!

title: So close
body:
I love TickTick as it gets almost everything right. Unfortunately, the drawbacks matter to me enough to take 2 stars away.

Pros:
1) Competitive price
2) Quick and functional
3) Simple to learn/use across platforms
4) Some customizability
5) Overall has all the basics down pretty well

Cons:
1) Calendar events are tasks. You have to mark them as done/completed. I just want a Calendar event to be a Calendar event. A time-block, a reminder, I don't know.
2) Sync malfunctions quite frequently between widgets-iOS-macOS. Not calendar sync, just in general the tasks often fail to sync properly across devices and/or widgets.
3) Design is a bit dated, but not so bad that I'd take a star off for this.

title: App is OK, support and service is subpar
body: I used the app for a few months and purchased the subscription. I use it primary for scheduling tasks at work so I used the Outlook calendar integration. It was working fine, good not great, until an update made it where the calendar settings were never saved so it kept syncing a bunch of calendars I didn’t want and was showing them in places I had turned them off. I submitted a ticket and got a quick response - they have always responded quickly initially. My ticket was reporting the issue and asking how to revert versions until it was addressed. That request was never answered - it’s been months, I have replied to it again asking for help, and it just sits there “In process” with no response from support. I finally gave up and went to Amazing Marvin (which is amazing) and was ready to cancel TickTick. When I reached out to support request a refund I was informed that the issue was fixed and was past the 14 day window from purchase to apply for a refund. The original ticket was never updated, the issue never seemed to go away, but when I asked (and was denied) for a refund, I’m told it’s now fixed. TickTick should hold themselves to the same standards - if I can only apply for a refund within 14 days, it shouldn’t take you more than 14 days to acknowledge a reply to a ticket.

title: So helpful for my adhd
body:
I started using this to have a todo list I could check off items directly from my smartwatch.  It’s turned into my daily to do and time tracking app.  I track my time and am able to invoice based off project, or give a breakdown on what I have been working on.  I started using this feature with a personal art project and now I mostly use it to track my work time, I can hit the start and stop button to track time, or if I forget to hit start I can go back and add the time in later.  You can set the time for a day, week or however long to see where your time is going, it has a nice pie chart with color coding and a great list that lists projects or to do items or tags and tells you exactly how much time was spent on each.. you can organize it however you want.  I saw my first two creative projects I had spent 20 plus hours on and was hooked after that, time tracking isn’t my strong suit, especially in hyper focus mode so it was nice to see exactly how much time those projects took.  You can also estimate how much time a task will take, I don’t use that like I thought I would. 

I love the calendar, my outlook has been deleting meetings for some reason, I look at this calendar because these ghost meetings show up in this.  I also really love the calendar view to add in quick to do’s.  On the weekly view I can add in things as I think of them throughout the day, this is great for my adhd tendencies and I love being able to click done and see everything I did that day or grab a task and move it to tomorrow or next week.  So easy to move.

Because I’m in this app regularly tracking my time or looking at the calendar it reminds me of my habit tracking, this app is regularly the reason I remember to take my supplements. I have also set it to remind me several times throughout the day to take a drink of water or relax my shoulders and take a few deep breaths.  This seems simple but I struggle with these still, even with reminders, although reminders help me remember I can take 20 seconds to breathe intentionally, and being able to check it off is the small dopamine incentive that gets me to do these things a lot of the time. 

I hear pomodoros are amazing for adhd, it was today that I actually decided I will try that feature in this app. 

It’s also gratifying to be able to look at the time window,  I started this in December 2023 and now I can look at the year view and see most days I have tracked time.  It’s so satisfying and I know if the beginning of the year was blank it would bother me.

title: The Best Calendar/To-Do List App Ever!!!
body: This really is the best app like this ever. It is layed out and organized exactly how I want it to be and it has all the functions I desire in a calendar/To-Do app. I love the way you can nest folders, lists, and items on your lists, and the time-tracking/activity logs and habit sections. I have tried almost every app like this and most don’t even come close to containing all the features I want or to being as organized and also as organized to look at and use as this one. It has an interface that makes sense to me and isn’t confusing or disorganized or cluttered or unappealing to look at like some of the other apps I’ve tried. Although it did take me a while to figure out how to best use some of the features - it wasn’t too bad, they have help articles and I was also trying to get it to work in a way for me that is more complicated than most people would want or need anyways, but after sitting with it for a few hours one day I was able to do what I wanted with it and organize my life and schedule in the way that works best for me and that is what made me super excited about this app, because it is the only calendar app that I have ever been able to do that with. However, you can happily use the app without doing any of that and I have often done that during times in my life when I didn’t care about viewing my tasks a certain way or using the Kanban style or Eisenhower Matrix, because it is easy to add tasks and habits and track your time and view them all without using any extra features. So although I often happily use the app without the pro plan (because I am pretty low-income with a lot of expenses), I prefer to pay for the pro plan when I can afford to because then the app is even better, but the non-pro version is very good also and I appreciate that so much. Tick Tick has pretty much become the only productivity app I use anymore.

title: Good but could use a few improvements
body:
UI took a little getting used to but has some great functionality. 
As for improvements. Foremost, needs an “Turn off overdue” or “Optional” setting for individual items. Like Yes I forgot or didn’t have time to do an item yesterday on my schedule, but it’s on repeat for today anyways. It shouldn’t have an overdue reminder unless the user wants it. 
Secondly, there are items that mag not have a specific due date or be on repeat. These are primarily for tasks that are crucial but would be nice if I had spare time. However, with a schedule these are items don’t show up anywhere so it’s easy to forget about them. There should be section for these tasks to should up on the day-to-day planner so if I finish all my priorities I can be reminded.
Lastly, once an item is complete for today, the item for rescheduled for tomorrow shouldn’t show. It’s annoying how many times I’ve accidentally clicked a future task as completed because it’s not clear and it doesn’t show up the next days schedule so I forget.

title: First day and it’s already changed my life
body:
I’ve had this app for not even 1 full day, and I’m already in LOVE with it. 

I liked todoist to help me schedule things just by typing out the what and when, but still struggled to coordinate my to do list with my calendar. Trying to use google calendars to sort tasks is a joke. And I love notion for big plans and organizing complex information, but it’s easy to make a mess of it and its not very user friendly for quick tasks, notes, and ideas. And again, calendar integration is lacking there. 
I usually use notes app (apple) to quickly jot stuff down, but then that gets really messy and unorganized as well, making it very easy to forget things. Plus, I can’t pull up my notes app on my PC, so I end up using a different notepad there, and then information is eventually in a million places. 

But with Tick Tick, I can do almost EVERYTHING I need to do in order to stay organized, manage my scattered thoughts and ideas in one place, integrate my google calendars, and ensure I don’t have to look at a million apps. 

Phew. I’ve never felt so compelled to write an app review, but I’m just so glad I found this app!!
