Imagine having to do that to five tasks. That’s 25 clicks. Why would they do that? You click on the task name and all you get is an empty page with the task name on it and its due date. No way to change anything on this page. Total wast of space. You have to click on the date in order to get to the page where you can set another date. 
Then you click on the date you want to set it to, and then you have to click on ‘done’ which goes back to the previous page, and then you have to click on ‘exit.’ And voilà ! Five clicks later, you just changed the date from yesterday to today.

I am able to establish healthy habits so much easier. My life is objectively much better having this app in it. I am a happier person than I was before finding this app, specifically because of this app. The closest I came to this state of being previously was achieved by carrying a small notepad and pen with me to organize my thoughts and tasks. This works even better because it takes up way less footprint, has integrated reminders, and endless long-term scheduling capabilities. If you are tired of wasting time with fractured time management, and are finally serious enough to REALLY TRULY IRON YOUR LIFE OUT, GET WORK DONE, and STOP LOSING TRACK OF THINGS OR FEELING OVERWHELMED, GET THIS APP. You will not regret it.

title: I love this app.
body:
I love this app, so much that I’ve been forced to write up a review. It’s been thoughtfully made to almost every degree. Getting starting can be a bit over whelmed as there are countless ways to personalize your experience. 

I would like to request the team to add a widget for Iwatch and iPhone that allows you to start a timer, of your choice, choosing from today, ALL task, INBOX, and / next 7 days list. 
Focus to do app (is far behind you guys) but they have a widget for iwatch that quickly allows for timing projects of your choice. 

As I try and track where my time is most often being spent, quick use of the timer and pom is essential. 

I also HATE, that the time has to be pressed to start after choosing the task. It would be great if this was an option in the settings. Many times I’ve chosen a task and didn’t realize the timer never started! (Despite having automatic start after break on in settings)

Over all this is an amazing app.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Everything works well. I mainly use this for tasks and calendar. All the matrix, pomodoro, habit stuff seems too finicky and clutters up the app way too much. 

However, overall it works except for the widgets. I’m not sure if it’s just on my end, but they don't update. If I get a notification of a task and I click on and clear it in the app it doesn’t update on the widget on my Home Screen. 

Also, I use 2 of the widgets, the calendar and the task. If I clear something on the tasks, it doesn’t clear/update on the calendar and vice versa. It’s extremely annoying. I have to click in and out of the app several times for it to work. The best part about having 2 widgets for me is that I see things at a quick glance, but if things aren’t clearing and I have other tasks, I won’t see them because there’s not enough space anyway. 

If they clear this up soon it’ll be perfect for me, but for now it’s not something I want to continue paying for.

body: I started out using the free version of TickTick because it had an easy way to utilize an Eisenhower Matrix (my preferred method of prioritizing tasks at work). Compared to apps like ToDoist, it feels restrictive and unhelpful. However, the tags, categories, language recognition, ability to assign pomodoro timers to specific tasks for task completion time tracking, satisfying notification sounds, and ease of adding tasks easily make up for it. If you’re someone who unintentionally forgets things, this app is definitely worth a try.

title: I always come back
body:
I have had a love hate relationship with ticktick. Mostly because of how good it is but wanting features that would make it the best calendar/task app on the app store.

What it does great:
1) great input method for tasks
2) reliable it has never once failed me or not notified me of a task
3) syncs very quickly to watch app
4) custom colors RGB!!!
5) themes! (Application could be better though.)

Things that would make it a lot better:
1) new task views, it looks outdated. Cluttered. Not good.
2) lack of event vs. task. Im so tired of having to go back and check off events that i did because they’re all considered tasks with checkboxes. Not good with people who have adhd.
3)no progress bar watch app like tiimo or calendars.
4)no custom fonts
5)no custom sound notifications
6)no 2 way sync with apple calendars. This is the biggest reason why ive stopped using ticktick in the past.

title: Best Personal Task Management
body:
TickTick is a great middle ground for simplicity and power. If you struggle to use other task apps you’ll likely find a home here. 

It’s affordable. The setup is straightforward. It has language recognition for quick entries. You can forward emails to make them into tasks in TickTick allowing you to keep your inbox empty. You can upload a variety of attachments, create sub tasks, take notes, convert notes to tasks, take a bullet point or list and quickly turn them into a series of tasks, integrate your calendar(s), make calendar events tasks (optional), and more. The mobile app works great. Desktop app works great. Pretty much flawless all around. 

If you’re looking to manage teams there are deeper apps out there; I would recommend something like Monday.com, Asana or ClickUp. For personal use, this is the best I have come across and I have been in this market for years.

title: I’m taking back my own strengths and gaining more!
body:
I would like to thank the developers of TickTick. Not too long ago; I was deemed permanently disabled. I became very depressed due to non activities or activities I could no longer participate in. I lost my drive, my passion, and most of all my brain fog made it almost impossible for me to stay on task and focus. Time management since the illness was almost gone completely. My therapist and docs suggested to find a motivation app and or a time management app. So I downloaded several, using the different features from several different apps. In which, if you are depressed, like me; it was overwhelming to navigate. Now, I have TickTick and no more opening more than one app! It’s all right here and best of all!  It is so customizable to your personal strengths and weaknesses. I was able to regain my strengths and just maybe make them more stronger than before my illness! My weaknesses? Well, they too have become strengths or I am working on them. I have hope that they will be able to become strengths in the future. Thanks to TickTick! I definitely would recommend this app; to anyone needing help to streamline your  days or just needing a friendly reminder to help keep you on track! I have even downloaded the app on my son’s phone! It helps us keep track of projects, homework, schedules, meetings and more! I also love that it reminds us to be and stay healthy! 
So thanks again! -MJ 

P.s.-take control on your own happiness and health! Physically, mentally and emotionally. As TickTick says “make yourself a priority.” 

You can do that and much more with this gem!

title: Best productivity for my ADHD brain
body:
I had undiagnosed ADHD for decades. I knew I had a problem organising my thoughts. I knew I was a sucker for “Shiny new things”. It took me a lot longer to realise all productivity apps worked but at some point I’d grow bored, overwhelmed, spend more time playing with the app than using the app. Then I discovered I had ADHD and knew why I had behaved the way I had, but now I was armed with really important knowledge of how my mind worked within the framework of ADHD. I did some research, revisited all the tools I’d used over the past decade - just about every app that appears in the top 10 lists. I shortlisted three and settled on TickTick for the following reasons.

Pomodoro built in. Before diagnosis, I used this technique to do the really hard, boring but necessary tasks my brain really didn’t want me to do. Now I use it to get a better understanding of how I spend my time. I’m hopeless at estimating how much time something will take. 
Habits. I put repeatable activities into the habit tracker but keep the numbers low. If I don’t then the real stuff doesn’t get done. In the past, I’d add dozens of small repeatable activities - things I was doing anyway - tick them off and see that I’d finished 80% of my tasks but the reality was, I wasn’t doing the stuff that really needed doing.
Sub tasks in sub tasks in subtasks . . . Breaking the impossible down into bite size chunks is a good strategy for everyone. For me, it keeps the lists small. Keeps me focused on what has to be done. I’m wired to look for novel and interesting. There’s nothing interesting about a big hard task but if I break it down then it becomes more interesting. Having multiple layers of sub tasks really helps me as long lists are just daunting and boring.
Completed view - I have a period of reflection, sometimes at the end of the day, sometimes first thing in the morning. Seeing what I did the previous day is a great incentive and helps me plan for the coming day. 
Works with third parties especially email. I keep my mail box empty. I can waste a huge amount of time on email. It can derail my productivity. So when I see an email that needs actioning, I add it to TickTick and archive the email. Move on. It’s on the inbox of TickTick and can be processed there like any other todo list item. Most emails are other peoples todo items, so processing them in a productivity app rather than email makes much more sense to me.

There are a whole bunch of other reasons but most of them are found in similar apps . . .works everywhere - on my phone, tablet, desktop, web. Etc.

title: The missing link between a task list and a project manager
body: I’ve been trying productivity apps, task lists and project managers for over thirty years. From the clumsy Franklin Covey digital planners to GTD methodology apps, I’ve tried them all. I’ve used Things from launch and Asana from the early days. I’ve tried Monday, Pagico, Notion, Opus One, Planmore, Jira, Basecamp, Trello and a long list of task lists. I can tell you this App is unique. It’s build up from simplicity to complexity and not the other way around. The consequence is that you feel you have a solid engine behind a minimalist interface allowing you to be highly productive without assuming the role of the “project manager”, a guy who does not create value but knows how to handle a certain tool. They are very close to achieve Nirvana; if they can create a share / collaboration ecosystem they might galvanize the productivity apps category.

title: all the necessary features without paywall
body:
what I needed:
- cross platform sync 
- easy categorization
- clean, easy interface
- home screen widget

Ticktick has all of it for free, plus:
- easy information input (just typing what I need is so much faster than selecting options 100 times over)
- tag view and list view 
- calendar view for mobile (not desktop, but understandable)
- habit tracking
- good search function

I felt genuine relief when I realized this actually worked well, after downloading and deleting dozens of worse apps.
I would even consider buying a plan in the future, which I would never do for an app that paywalled the most basic features.

title: Game changer
body:
A few years back I tried every popular task app there was. This is the one. I have everything in here, from camping lists, to daily to-do lists, to projects, to wishlists. The fact I can set a date for everything is amazing. The second best feature is the ability to create sublists. The very best feature is the ability to collaborate. My husband and I haven’t had an argument over groceries in years and we are always on the same page. It never used to be that way. It’s $3 a month but it is very worth it. 

The only feature I’d like, if it’s even possible, is the ability to tell Siri my reminders and then have them inserted directly into this app, rather than the iOS reminders. Might be possible with IFTTT or some other API but if it is possible, it hasn’t been obvious to me how to do it. Same with syncing with my iOS calendar.

body: TickTick’s price point is way better than any of its competitors, many of whom charge well more than triple the cost of TickTick Premium. title: Perfect, everything I dreamed of and more
body: As an overworked college student with ADHD and hella anxiety, I was suffering from major burnout. Since downloading this app, I still have 99 problems but my to do list isn’t one of them! My favorite feature is how the app is designed: you dump all of your tasks into your inbox, and from there you can organize as much or as little as you need. Want to organize your to dos by class, day, or priority? Done. Want to set notification times for some reminders but not others? Done. Want to see what you need to do today without worrying about everything else? Go right ahead. Want to set a pomodoro timer that gives you a lil’ tomato when you finish a cycle? They have that too! I don’t know why it’s a tomato, but it gives me the dopamine that my brain simply does not have on its own. I don’t want to bore anyone with a full synopsis of the app; just know, that FOR FREE, it has every feature you could possibly need, without being overwhelming. The design is sleek, simple, and probably perfect. Just try it, it has helped me so so much.

title: Great product!
body:
Update Nov 2023:  I’m still very happy with TickTick and also appreciate the recent user interface improvements such as the partial view when opening a task versus taking up entire screen when opening.  I use TickTick primarily on my phone so space is limited and this feature helps to see and do more things quickly.  I have a feature request though which is to have some sort of list or template that can contain a numerical field and have a summation of those numbers within that list.  Reason for request is that I use TickTick to track my daily spending and as of now, I manually tally each charge into a running total which I then reconcile at the end of the month when I pay my bills.  It would be nice if this was somewhat automated so I wouldn’t need to do the manual calculation for the all-up tally every time I have a charge.  Not a huge deal since just adding or subtracting charges from my monthly total but would save some time and effort if had this automated in a list somehow.  

Original post:  I’ve been using TickTick for about a year now, and it has helped tremendously in making my life more efficient and productive. Before TickTick, I would keep all my TODO lists in a spreadsheet, and even with storing the spreadsheet in the cloud so I could access anytime on my phone, it was very cumbersome to work with. TickTick’s streamlined way of making and managing lists is a true time saver. Also, having the historical context of all my completed items has come in handy when at times I needed to grab the details from a task I already completed. Beyond these things, having an integrated calendar alongside my tasks helps me better see and manage a ‘big picture’. Previous to TickTick, I used my email’s calendar which was ok but I couldn’t integrate easily with the spreadsheet I was using for my TODOs and therefore made it harder to manage things I had to get done on a day to day basis. Finally, the cost is much lower than most other similar task and calendar based tools. I wasn’t originally focused on the price point since I was mainly looking for the right feature set but the lower price was an added bonus.

title: Does everything and it just works!
body:
This might be the only app that does everything I want it to do, and isn't full of bugs. 
Some of my favorite features:

*Adding subtasks (and subtasks for your subtasks...it's subtasks all the way down)
*Powerful tag and filter functionality
*Extensive control over how you view tasks and lists etc
*A great range of color options for lists/tasks/calendars/etc
*Built-in productivity tools like Pomodoro timer and Eisenhower matrix
*A full-feature calendar with multiple view options like list (with timeline view option), day, 3-day, week, and month view that integrates with existing calendars (Google, iPhone, etc)
*Location-based reminder function
*Constant reminder option
*Habit tracking
*Smooth vertical calendar scrolling!!!
*So far I haven't encountered a single bug. It's so rare for an app with this many features to just work and not ever crash.

Thank you Ticktick team for adding smooth vertical calendar scrolling, which I asked for a while back and you delivered! I can't tell you how happy this made me lol.

title: Just what I needed
body:
I’m 39 and work in tech as a product designer. I’ve had ADHD all my life and have struggled to find ways to cope. Lists and pomodoro timers have been helpful in the past. I stumbled across this app and got excited. 

TickTick ties together my to-do list and my precious pomodoro timer in one place. This helps me stay focused. But with the calendar sync and the priority view, I've been able to get ahead. I lead our team sprint plan on Fridays. I copy over my weekly work tasks. Furthermore, I add my next week of personal items during the weekend. By Monday morning, I've time blocked most of my week. If I can get it in TickTick it will get done, or I won't forget it.  

The app is intuitive and easy to use. It has a surprising amount of depth, however. Tags and folders as well as timeline views let me nerd out and organize my life. And I am enjoying digging into my stats. 

I would like it if I could easily click a meeting invite from Teams and open it from TickTick. A simpler way to sync with ADO would be nice too. I would be curious about how they handle AI in the future. I've seen other apps that work to protect your tome with AI. 

All that said, this is an amazing tool for me and well worth the price. It's something I use every day.

title: The best task and schedule program I’ve tried, with one frequently irritating issue
body:
First let me say, I love Tick Tick. I’ve been using the premium version for years, and nothing else comes close. I love having my task lists and calendar all in one app, and the pomodoro timer is just a bonus. It also has very good natural language processing that I use for scheduling future events and tasks, which is something a surprising number of similar apps are lacking. 

My only major complaint is a bug where I will swipe or check off a certain task, only for it to register a completely different task as being checked off. This has been a consistent issue for a long time. It’s not a huge deal if I’m checking off a task and the wrong one ends up getting crossed off — I’ll just undo it. It becomes a bigger problem when I delete something and it randomly deletes something else instead, especially if I don’t notice it in time and end up having no idea what the deleted task was. 

I’ve still given this app five stars because it is genuinely closer to perfect than any other task app I’ve ever used, but I would love to see that issue fixed. 

(I’d also love to see more customization options for the color scheme/themes!)

title: The Best Productivity App on the Market
body:
I’m a huge fan. I bounced around to a handful of different individual apps/app combos. This is the best one available. Normally don’t give five stars, but TickTick has become my main source of productivity tracking. I initially downloaded it as an alternative to Apple Reminders (which is very restricted); however, it also took over my usage of Apple Calendars and Stride (goal tracking). It also does a fine job of tracking daily habits and keeping time logs. 

If I were to offer feedback:
1. Make Manual Time Tracking more accessible
2. Turn the “+” (add button) into an action button. Hold down the “+” button to allow the user to toggle adding tasks, undo/redo actions, and speech-to-task additions. 
3. Add to the integrations section of settings (would love to add integrations with N8N & Notion more natively). 
4. Somehow integrate two-way sync support for native Apple apps (Apple Reminders and Apple Notes) to mimic the way TickTick does Apple Calendar. 
BONUS: Add dependencies to the Timeline View. Would be a game changer. 

I am a strict evaluator on the App Store. Truly one of the hidden gems & I am glad the TickTick team is on top of updates and constantly improving the app on a daily basis. Good work!

title: Fantastic All-in-One Productivity App
body:
It’s been about 2 years and I’m loving this app. I spent all of my free time for four days straight searching for an app that had all the features I needed in one place. 
Loved features: 
-An integrated calendar 
-a todo list viewable in conjunction with calendar “today view” 
-a habit tracker that provides streaks and statistics 
-a timer/ stopwatch for focus and productivity 
-shareable or collaborative capabilities 
This app has that plus a few other bonuses that I didn’t know I wanted. I went ahead and paid for the annual subscription which was reasonably priced. (I do wish there was an option to pay once for lifetime use, but I’m not complaining.) There are a few tweaks that I would love to see that would make the app absolutely perfect for me. 
Would love to see: 
-an option to view all habit statistics together instead of each one individually. 
-an option for “less is better” for habit breaking. 
-an option to share a combined statistical summary of habit progress for accountability partnering. 
-an option to add events to integrated calendar from the app that syncs out to that calendar instead of just in. 
-an option for reoccurring reminders on notes instead of having to reset them each time. 
-lap options on the stopwatch 
Those are my observations and suggestions so far. I appreciate that there is an in-app location for reporting issues and making suggestions. Each time that I have used it, they responded within 24 hours and were friendly. Also, it seems that they are continuing to make upgrades and feature adds to make this app even better than it already is. Absolutely wonderful job on this app! 
Appreciatively, 
Janise.
P.s. I am a real customer. I was not paid or incentivized in any way to write this review. I did not received the app for free and was not asked to try it out. Just putting that out there because when I read reviews sometimes I wonder if they are real or not.

title: This is the app I’ve been waiting for!
body:
I’ve been a purveyor of task management systems for a long time, yet despite my beautifully categorized and filtered list views on Asana, then later AirTable (which I still love for managing larger projects and databases) I just kept finding myself going back to my lame notepad on my iPhone to coordinate to do lists and wish lists in my personal life so I could collaborate with my husband with more condensed information. I even tried “calendar chunking” where I would block out time to work on different categories of tasks, but having 2 small kids made creating a consistent schedule basically impossible. On top of it, none of my systems were good at managing sub tasks, while making sure I’m saving enough time for day to day healthy habits like exercise, cooking, reading, etc.

Then comes TickTick. I did a lot of research before investing time into building up an app, and I’m so glad I landed on this one. It takes all of the best parts of project management systems, to-do lists, notepads, calendars, and habit trackers and smashes them into one beautiful interface. 

The lists are easy to navigate and I love that I can easily move tasks up or down the list or assign items to sub categories. The ability to filter views and/or group tasks by priority, date due, name etc makes it easy to determine what my biggest priorities are, and helps me to avoid committing to doing too much each day. Finally, the ability to see my tasks for the day on a calendar, right next to my existing appointments AND habit reminders helps me keep everything balanced and achievable.

Another critical item for me was to be able to share lists with my husband (for grocery shopping lists, tracking home projects, naming records we want to buy, bucket lists, etc.) the best part about a lot of these types of lists is that you can set them to not appear in your “to-do list”, and instead they are just lists there for you to jot stuff down that you want to track but won’t remember later.

I’ve been using it for about a week, and I’ve already gotten so many things done because I’m focusing on 2-3 critical items a day, while also seeing what I either need to delegate or just not prioritize (which is almost as critical as actually doing things.) In addition, I have so much more awareness of my daily habit goals, and I’m more consistent with all of them now.

The only minor thing I wish this system had was a way to estimate the amount of time a task or sub task will take, and then be able to see the full amount of estimated time scheduled tasks will take within a given list, view, or calendar period. However, this is because I’m the kind of person who likes to have an idea of when I can take a deep dive on bigger projects or make major pushes to change the course of my life, and I want to have a realistic timeline to plan and prioritize it. For the vast majority of my purposes though, this app has everything I need.

title: A perfect fit
body:
TickTick has been amaze balls! I’ve tested a number of apps. Mostly been working with Asana since 2014. Been testing alternatives on and off for a couple years and hadn’t found anything worth switching for. Asana and others like it have too many features and not the specific ones I find more useful. I want it simple, clean, and with the best features for my personal workflow. 

TickTick is the first time I’ve had an app actually help me be more productive. It is showing up at the right time for me. I knew exactly what I wanted and it has it. 

The integrated calendar is a must. Who wants to write things in one app then do it again when time blocking? So annoying to double planning and organization time. I’ve tried combining apps and linking them but I had to have one that does exactly what this one does. 

The Eisenhower matrix is also extremely helpful. Another very useful tool seamlessly integrated. 

The habit tracker is great. I used habit bill for years but when it’s right alongside my work it is much easier to keep my eye on what need to get done. 

Amazing Marvin also has these elements and is also a clean aesthetic (less visual overwhelm), but it didn’t work intuitively. Amplenote is an awesome concept, but when it came time to use it, it was visually overwhelming and required too many steps to get things done in the app. And it is so dull looking I couldn’t do it. Like it was designed in the 90’s for a large corporation. Nothing wrong with that but if I’m going to use the app and look at it many times throughout the day I have got to like the visual aesthetics. 

Conclusion: know what you want and why you want it, don’t compromise on the top features you want, find an app that does that, get more done.

title: Everything I’ve been looking for...almost
body:
TL;DR it’s a great to-do app for collaborating!

I came to TickTick after having used Microsoft To-Do (and Wunderlist before that). I used those apps primarily for collaborating on grocery shopping and household to-do lists with my spouse. Wunderlist was perfect for us, but was eventually shut down. The app’s developers suggested Microsoft’s To-Do as an alternative, and that worked, but there were two frustrating and ultimately deal-breaking issues:

a. Syncing lists between me and my spouse was very unreliable and inconsistent. I would often return from grocery shopping to discover that my spouse had added items that didn’t show up on my end. 

b. Rearranging items on list would sometimes cause an item to move up to the next nested level’s list. There would be no way to move the item back, except to delete and re-enter the item.

TickTick was the only app that offered key features we were looking for:

1. Fast and reliable syncing between collaborators

2. Lists that can be organized into categories

3. The ability to nest sub-tasks within a list’s to-do item

4. Glitch-free editing and rearranging of items in a list

In addition to fulfilling the above four requirements, I also appreciate TickTick’s clean and minimalist interface. It makes it easy to quickly find items while herding my kids at the grocery store

I also find the Apple Watch functionally useful, but flawed. Lists can be viewed on an Apple Watch, eliminating the need to constantly take my phone out of my pocket. But the lists on Apple Watch do not preserve any categories, so items are listed in seemingly random order. It would be ideal if Apple Watch lists showed categories as well, or at least preserved the order of items from the iPhone app.

title: Truly life changing
body:
Okay I want to preface this by saying 1. I never ever write reviews for apps and 2. I didn’t receive any incentive, payment or benefits for writing this. I’m always sus of people who write amazing reviews so I want to make that clear

I have ADHD and I have tried every to do list/productivity app that exists. I would get super excited about them and spend hours setting them up and then give up a week later. I fully expected the same to happen with this. It’s been two months now and I use this daily and my productivity has sky rocketed.

I will say, I think you need the premium version to fully understand how good it is. There are so many features and I love that I can have the habit tracker, to dos separated by areas of my life (work, home, school), and calendar reminders all in one place. I also love how customizable the app itself is in terms of background image, icons etc. You can also set tasks to repeat at certain intervals (ex water plants every Sunday), or by day of the week (take out trash every Monday). 

I think the most motivating part for me is the little ping sound that it makes when you complete a task lol. I need the dopamine hit and hearing that makes me want to do more so I can feel rewarded by the sound. It’s stupid but it works. 

I don’t think I have any negatives on this besides the fact that you need to pay for a yearly subscription (I think $30) rather than a once, life long subscription. But I will keep paying because it’s the only one that works for me. 

Please please please never take away this app!!!

title: Pretty happy with TickTick 😊
body:
TickTick has been awesome for me. It’s like multiple apps in one, while maintaining simplicity. Works well with GTD (Getting Things Done) approach. 

My self-improvement goal was to be more efficient and effective. So things like time management, task management, dynamic prioritization, etc. 

I tend to be easily overwhelmed by my anxiety condition. It would make me stress if there are too many things happening, or if I have to spend too much screen time. That’s why I stopped using Notion and some other heavy apps. 

Other competitors seemed to be Todoist and Apple’s Reminders. They were both okay for me, but I wished they had a few more functionalities I wanted. 

Thankfully, I came across TickTick when someone recommended it on TeamBlind. I got excited when it had Pomodoro timer or stopwatch option with a Focus goal so you can set intentional small goals to make progress. You can even set estimated Pomodoro time for future tasks hehe

The app also had the Eisenhower Matrix and tags/filters, which greatly help organize my sheer volume of random thoughts that come up every few minutes. 

The app has a ton of other great functionalities too, and I’m very happy with the TickTick’s mindset of empowering the user to get things done. 

I’d like to thank the TickTick team very much for helping me declutter my life and manage my anxiety level with this app and the team’s valiant efforts! 🥰

title: Ridiculous that it removes reminders from reminders app
body:
Seems like it could be a useful app, but it is beyond stupid to have it automatically delete your reminders from your reminders app if you have them automatically import from reminders. It makes the app completely useless to me. There is absolutely no value in not letting users decide this; I need my reminders in my reminders app for various uses that this app can’t meet, so having it automatically delete any new reminders I create makes this app completely useless.

Edit: In response to the developer response: I am aware that you can turn off auto-import from reminders. What you can’t do is have auto import from reminders *on*, without the app deleting your reminders from the reminders app. Meaning there is no way to have your reminders synced between both apps the way you can with apps like Fantastical.

title: Almost perfect
body:
I would love to rate this with 5 stars, but to me it’s lacking the key feature of FREE email integration (developers, please correct me if I am wrong). 

I do LOVE this app for all the things it does well for me. It is a quick and easy set up and it provides for the ability to import iOS Reminders. The app is simple and clean, and very intuitive. Most things people need are available in free version, but even the premium isn’t too exorbitant. 

The one drawback is email integration. From everything that I have read and attempted, you must use the Spark app as an integration point between TickTick and email if you want to send an email over to TickTick as a task. I could get on board with that, if it were free or even cost effective. But it is by no means cheap at 7.99/month or $59.99/year. Don’t get me wrong, I am not knocking Spark at all. I have never used their app and never thought I needed an app to manage my email. So I am swilling to concede that their pricing is reasonable for all the services they provide. However, $60 a year is quite expensive to just have the ability to convert an email to a task. 

I believe the email integration is something that TickTick has the ability to provide for free or as part of their premium services just as other task managing apps do. I have chosen TickTick as the app to use after trying numerous others as their service provides everything else I need. But I don’t quite understand why they don’t or haven’t built email integration as part of their native app, when they clearly have a great product and that option would make them stand out even further.

title: Great app - but how secure is it?
body:
Giving credit where it’s due the TickTick App is definitely one of the best designed, with the best features of apps out there! Most apps in the store can’t really hold a candle to it in comparison of features/functionality, not to mention the ability to make use of GTD.

All that said, I’d be amiss if I didn’t call out that this application is one that is designed, coded, and while hosted within AWS, is technically owned by the State of China through the regime. The TickTick app shares a code base with that of the Chinese-branded “Ticklist” app (and is documented as such on their non-US website). 

Again, great app, and love the design, just can’t trust that the app is as secure as it claims. Especially when you take into consideration that it automatically sync’s to “the cloud” with no alternative secured/local storage option (like you see in other todo apps - like Things 3, OmniFocus, 2Do, etc.).
author: Demosthenes

title: TickTick is Superior!
body: Over the years, I’ve tried ALL of the major to-do apps. Each was great in its own way, but each had at least one major restriction. I thought that I’d have to “settle” for one of them and used each for at least one year (and up to five years). When I could no longer take the awkwardness of design or the lack of a needed feature, I started looking again. How had I missed TickTick? I downloaded it. For almost a year, I refused to write a review. It worked very well but something was missing. That missing part was taking sufficient time to learn what the developers had done. They didn’t set up a system for me to follow. They set up a system that is so innovative that it conforms to my needs in multiple ways. When I took sufficient time to study it, I was overwhelmed with the thought that they put into it. I had set it up incorrectly, so I deleted my first attempt and started anew. I can now accomplish so much more without the pressure that had been placed on me by the other to-do lists. TickTick is everything that I have ever wanted in this category of apps. I’m so grateful! If you pass over this app or download it without patiently learning the details of its features, you will miss a true gem.

I have the Eisenhower Matrix, weekly calendar, and shopping list as widgets on my home screen, so every time I open my phone then I know what I need to do.

title: Don’t make me think
body:
It’s hard to articulate exactly why I’ve come to loathe this app, but let me try, as succinctly as I can:

Every time I open the app, I get confused.

Maybe this is early onset dementia or something, but maybe the UI could use some refinement.

I think that it tries to accomplish too much. Or maybe I try to get fancy and use features that I don’t need to build smart lists that confuse me further.

I have a smart list called “inbox unsorted” because I can’t accomplish what I need to with the regular inbox.

That’s just scratching the surface.

The app is overhyped. I think MKBHD jumped on the bandwagon for whatever reason, and now everyone thinks the app is great.

It’s really not.

Stop making me think. Get bigger tap targets. Allow me to hide items from my inbox that have already been tagged, by default.

title: Simple and powerful
body:
Easy to use, with tons of functionality for advanced use cases. Some of the things I use and like:
- Markdown formatting
- Notes, Recurring tasks and subtasks
- Calendar view for timeboxing everything and subscribing to my other calendars
- List and Tags
- Collaboration on lists shared w/ my wife
- Pomodoro timer for coding projects and school
- backlinks
- siri shortcuts
- pinned sticky notes

Only feature I really wish I had:
- Being able to time box habits on the calendar.  I have opted to make them all tasks instead, but you miss out on history log and completion progression that the habit interface gives.

Considering the amount of time I have struggled with finding an all in one productivity app over the years, this one is miles above the competition.  Love what you guys are doing.  If you need a backend dev, let me know, happy to help develop.

P.S. Eisenhower matrix is pretty rad, but I really need a process for switching to it and maintaining it.  Maybe a daily workflow that helped you schedule and prioritize would be possible?

title: Raving
body:
The tl;dr is this is a really good app, compared to apple reminders and one other I can’t remember lol

I am the kind of person who found it hard to relax because I had “so much to do today” and when I wanted to do work around the house, I’d feel overwhelmed with all the stuff I had to do, let alone set aside time for my side hobbies. 

Well, enter ticktick. 

I can hold the plus button to say “every monday at 8pm take out the trash” and will set a reminder every monday at 8pm, “take out the trash” you can do daily, weekly, monthly reminders. Heck, there is a section just for friend’s birthdays!

I can organize with multiple categories of tasks, so my house chores can be one category, my daily health and hygene can be another, my upcoming events can be another. 

And I can see all my tasks for the day in a handy “today” section. It doesn’t send push notifications until a task is past due.

 it’s totally free, unless you want to support the dev for 30$ a year, and then you get lots of interesting aesthetic ui reskins, and a handy calendar view for all your tasks. I choose to support the developers, but it’s really great that a tool that can help so many people doesn’t require payment. 

I am on the second week using this app, and while I’m not perfect at getting all tasks done, I’ve been so much more on top of things, and I’ve been less stressed during my relaxation time, not having to think about “all I have to do today”

title: Best Task Manager Ever

I also love the habit tracker and the built in pomodoro timer which once again eliminated the need for my habit tracking app (Habitica) and using my phone timer. The other thing I love is the calendar. Now instead of setting false deadlines and having to keep moving tasks back, I can just keep them on the list and pull them into the calendar when I have time. Really helps with time blocking and when you do pomodoros it puts the task you are working on and the pomodoros you spent on the, right in the calendar. Lastly it creates a summary page of all the week’s activities automatically. Great for weekly reviews and reflections. Other features I love:

title: Tried Them All (Literally)
body: I am a bit of a productivity junkie. I often watch TedTalks, read books and surf the web for the latest and greatest productivity hacks, tricks and apps. I have tried hundreds of apps from expensive mind mapping suites to top rated stand alone todo lists. Most did not disappoint, but they did leave room for improvement. It just seemed there was a feature missing that had to get covered by another app. I was in an infinite search for a solid all-in-one productive life tool. Enter TickTick! I use this app daily and I have not touched a single other productivity based app since downloading. If you are at all familiar with other todo lists, pomodoro timers, and calendar apps, you will be right at home here! It has it all, just like a Swiss Army knife. Things I love: - Siri Integration, don’t need IFTT or other outside apps to make it work. As in the philosophy of Apple, it just works! - Calendar view, I can finally eliminate a suite of calendar apps that clutter my phone! The agenda view helps to tie in all my daily priorities from around my accounts. - Cross platform sync, in my life it is essential to use the web, iPad, iPhone and Mac interfaces. They are all similar in their look/feel and the sync is almost instantaneous. -Pomo timer tool, it literally incorporates one of the best productivity tools out there! No longer is there a need to sync data with yet another app to help you focus, it is all included here! - Smart list filtering helps to customize your priority views. No longer do you have to use the preprogrammed options to display what you want. Simply use tags or unique features to pull out what is important to you! What it needs to develop: - Alexa (or Google Assistant) direct integration similar to Siri. Most people use a few of these and having the option for them all to channel back to one app would be amazing! - Themes, pretty basic stuff so far, just needs some more options. - Native language integration could use some beefing up. Thank You for making one of my forever top ten apps!

title: If you're a student you need this app
body:
I was hesitant to use this app because these kinds of apps don't tend to stick with me. I've tried everything (so many apps), being someone who struggles with a lot of executive functioning skills like remembering dates, deadlines, assignments, but mainly time management of my assignments/studying, and prioritizing. 

But this app has changed my life and has every feature I am looking for plus more. Premium version is definitely worth it if you are a student and you are struggling with any of the same things I mentioned above. It is more customizable than I expected and Tick Tick keeps coming out with new features that I never knew I would benefit from. Whoever did the UI/UX for this app, I have serious respect because I'm definitely your target customer, being an undergraduate college student, and it feels like you can read my mind. The timeline function is great for people who need visual reminders, and the fact that Tick Tick can link with your Google Calendar is...amazing. 

I would recommend this app to students, as I am an undergrad student, but I definitely see myself continuing to use it in the future. 

Unless I find a better to-do list app, but I'm doubtful because Tick Tick is perfect and I've been using it for a month now consistently along with my linked Google Calendar. I finally feel on top of my life. Give it a try.

title: Very capable app, but still needs some work
body:
I’m satisfied with most of the app’s features, but I think there are two main areas that could still use a lot of work: Dark mode and localization.

I exclusively use dark mode in every single app that I can. However, this is the first app that I’ve found that I actually prefer using the light mode for. Boundaries between different objects on the screen aren’t well optimized in dark mode and this makes it harder to use.

The English localization both in language as well as the persistence to upgrade to the paid version do a clear disservice to the app and to those interested in using it. There are issues in punctuation, spacing, and expression that signal to me that the localization team still has much work to do in understanding the target audience to create a polished product for many cultures outside of China.

TickTick has gained a lot more attention and I’d like to see it succeed, but I think it deserves more polish.

title: Best to-do app out there
body:
This is by far the best to-do app, and you don’t even need the Premium membership to experience its best features.

There are many widgets that allow you to see your tasks without opening the app, including calendar view and task view. You can also customize the widgets so that they show what you want to see (e.g. tags, lists, today view, etc.). 

To make sure you’re getting your tasks done, there’s a focus option that allows you to use a stopwatch or the Pomodoro technique to get your things done. I have recently started using this, and I’ve finished more than I expected.

You can also track your habits with this app, and there are great widgets for those as well. You can customize it to time done or just by completion, and there are many default options for habits to choose from.

But some great features are only with Premium, such as calendar view, the Eisenhower Matrix, some small customization features, and sounds during focus. 

But overall I would for sure recommend this app to anyone who’s struggling to keep up with their jobs, or even people who just want to organize their life better. Everything is integrated into this one app, and it’s been a game changer for me.

title: This one reminds & snooze reminds!
body: I have downloaded and removed so many reminder apps from my phone. They all remind me to do something but the reminder doesn’t stay visible & I end up missing it. This app is a blessing. I love the snooze feature so much. I can snooze a reminder for 15 minutes, an hour, or more, or mark it done. It’s so easy to add a reminder by pressing + and hitting send. Then, with one swipe, I can set what time and date I want it to remind. I love the widget that shows how many reminders are set for the day, so every time I open my phone, I see a red number telling me how many reminders there are. What a cool feature! I love the shopping list and I love that I can set reminder notification sounds to something I hear better. I can also change the background color to match my phone which is pretty. I just wish the premium features were offered at a one time lower fee. I don’t want to pay monthly and don’t want to pay the yearly amount. Overall, this is the best reminder app & I am so glad I found it. Finally! They got it right. 😊

title: Good but UI is inefficient for core usage
body:
I’m a premium subscriber, and this is about the iOS app primarily.

There isn’t a fast way to check a previous habit (eg one from yesterday). You have to go to the calendar, click the date and manually type in the value as the number Achieved! That’s WAY too much work when normally the habits are incremented up by 1. Maybe have it so when you tap the calendar date it increments by one, or if you hold it then the full page pops up? (With the “achieved” count). If you accidentally increment a habit, you can not decrease it/undo it, you can only reset it entirely. 

Also it appears that the habit tracking data is all online on the cloud, which makes it slow to bring up on my phone. 

Frankly the entire habit subsection that allows you to keep a ‘note log’ for each habit seems like a waste to me, given the issues with the rest of the app. But maybe that’s just me.. I was excited to have habits included so I could move away from the separate habit apps I used (Today and Streaks) but it’s needs to be faster/more efficient to use.

The other big UI issue is that there is no way to keep the sidebar open while viewing/editing your tasks/notes/lists. You can toggle it open but it almost fills the entire screen (which is unnecessary). A much better layout is how 2Do does it, with the sidebar open along with your tasks/lists, and there are several options to change the size and detail of the layout. 

Also to open the sidebar you have to first be in the task/list/notes section (so you must tap the bottom left corner) and then tap the upper left corner to reveal it. That’s a ton of work and thumb strain. You can technically swipe right on the left side to open it but that works very poorly (because swiping down reveals the search bar). 

You ought to be able to just swipe right anywhere to reveal the sidebar. The search bar should just be a separate button somewhere instead of swiping down. Accessing your task/list/notes quickly is far more important than searching!

This is a very promising app / service with great cross-platform support and many useful features lacking in other competing to-do apps, but they really need to prioritize improving efficiency of the core functionality on the phone app.

title: A todo, habit, and scheduling app all in one
body: I love this app. I went from Apple Reminders to Google Tasks to Todoist to TickTick. Here are the reasons I landed here (FYI I do pay for the pro version) - calendar integration - ability to drag and drop unscheduled tasks onto my calendar - ability to have different views (all, today, tomorrow, this week) that combine my calendar events and todos into chronological order - habit tracking - Eisenhower matrix (didn’t know what this was until I tried it, but I really like using it) - Works on every platform (iOS, Android, Mac, PC, Web) - Great for note taking and/or todos - List/Kanban view are both options - You can have multiple lists that can be complete or filtered in your other views (calendar, all, today, etc) There are other nice to haves like pomodoro, but I haven’t used it yet. The only con that I’ve found is that their API is really hard to authenticate to and use (their development docs are vague and unclear). I was able to get it working so that I could programmatically add tasks via a raspberry pi and what not. But it took a lot of work

title: Everything I Wanted
body: I downloaded every. single. to-do list app. And after upwards of two hours of combing through everything and comparing, I can confidently say TickTick is the best one out there. My favorite part of this app is how specific you can get with the organization. Put priority markers, put tags on each task, manually adjust the list. It makes things so much easier to help keep on track for the day. I also love the fact that you can set a list to be for task, for notes, or both. This, as well as how specific the organization can get, really helps you get the absolute most out of the free version. What really set this aside for me was how pleasant everything is to look at. There’s a good amount of color pallet options, even with the free version. I noticed that with most other apps like this is that it either look very bland and didn’t offer any options worth noting or it focused too much on appearance and began lacking in the actual functionality that brought you to the app in the first place. TickTick not only accomplished both well, but did so with an interface that is very easy to learn and use. Whether you want a list for yourself, or to share it with someone and keep things together, this is THE app.

title: Finally the perfect calendar/reminders/habit-tracker integration!
body: I have long yearned for a single, streamlined way to view everything I need to do in a day. Calendar events, reminders, one-off tasks, habits that don’t feel appropriate for the calendar nor reminders, etc. This is that app. It provides all the functionality that I could ever want to use, without being overwhelming. Stop looking at other options, you’ve found the one. Don’t let the subscription intimidate you, I’ve been using the free version for 2 months and I have never felt restricted. Pros: Calendar Integration: The integration into Apple calendar is astounding. Being able to not only view, but cross off calendar events is very satisfying. Habits: Keeping track of habits (up to 5 in the free version, perfect for me) is great! It keeps track not only of how many times I’ve done it, but what my success streak is. Best part: I can customize it so that if I only wanna do something on weekdays, I don’t lose my streak every weekend! Reminders: all the same functionality that the default reminders app has plus some, AND it’ll auto-import reminders to the app, so you can just tell Siri to remind you about something and tick-tick will pick it up! Amazing! Eisenhower Matrix: The Who-what? This thing is awesome! I had no idea what it was before this app, but it’s perfect. It sorts tasks into whether or not they are urgent and/or important, making it super easy to prioritize different tasks day-to-day! Other: there is a nice pomodoro timer that works well, I personally don’t use it but for those who are a fan of pomo stuff this will be great for you! Cons: Habits: the app unfortunately cannot force me to actually complete the tasks I want to get done every day, I’m going to have to wait for the robot uprising for that. Seriously, this app is awesome. Download it. Stop looking at other options, this is it

title: Great to-do app, but…
body:
I’d love to give this 5 stars.  I use it daily, and it really is the best to-do app I’ve used.  There’s one issue that keeps me from 5-stars. 
The price. 
I would like to upgrade to premium.  I absolutely would, as I think they do great work, and should be paid for it.  However, $3 a month, or $27 a year?!   That’s just too much. 
I have the best adblocker available, that I would be willing to pay those numbers for, but even that only cost a one time purchase of $3.  I’m not trying to sound cheap.  I just think a monthly/yearly payment is too much.  Even if it was $27 for the lifetime I would do it.  But yearly?  That’s too much.  It’s a bummer, because I like to change appearances and stuff, and I would gladly pay a more reasonable fee to do so.  But I also don’t see myself paying for the next 10-20 years to do so. I think there should be a one-time purchase option, and can’t believe there isn’t. Otherwise it’s great, but I’d really like to be able to do more.

title: Tik Tik is my most utilized App hands down
body:
I use it to hold me accountable in practicing good daily habits. My daily water intake has never been better. Tik Tik gets me to my water intake goal every day with spread out reminders to log my cupsso if I haven’t had water I chug some when I get a reminder to log my cups so I have something to log.

Love love love tick tick! Tried Noom to build good healthy habits and that’s what started me in this journey but I will be officially replacing Noom with Tik Tik because Tik Tik is super customizable and focuses on schedule and reminders while Noom is more like a daily mini course to keep your health goals relevant which for sure works. Just think Tik Tik is more for me, being the person that has always used daily planners, even as a child, to keep me on track. It combines all my calendars, notes, habit tracker/reminders, general reminders, works great with my iPhone reminder app. I have outlook for work synced to iPhone calendar which I use for personal stuff and not sure which calendar it syncs with but all my stuff get integrated nicely.

Tried Todoist, Structured and Anydo and although they each had their neat little think none of them had the habit tracker like this and as many user interface options (screen views).

I recommend this to anyone that is really busy and needs help managing their tasks to be more productive and have a balanced life. I work 80hrs a week sometimes, I like sports, exercising, reading, remembering to take my supplements, remembering to study for professional advancement, taking breaks from computer, wearing a retainer, drinking water but my health related items where taking a hit because when I work I get super tunnel vision and won’t even take a bathroom break or lunch. Tik Tik helps me take moments from my work to prioritize my health and social life better. Love this app!

title: Subtasks! Habits feature needs improvements:

I can organize everything in my life in a way that works with my brain! If subfoldering and subtasking is the way your brain works this app might work for you. 

I’ve started using the habits feature as well and it’s been helpful to keep track of and begin some good habits. I’ve given 4 stars only because the cumulative habits feature needs a little bit of work. It can be a little bit annoying to have to swipe then input the specific amount of completion. I’m someone who checks off tasks as soon as I complete them throughout the day. It would be nice if I could tap the little check box multiple times for each cumulative task rather than a once at the end of the day or fiddling with the record input feature each time.

title: This is THE ONE
body:
***Update:  after using this app since 12/2018,  there is nothing more that I can add to my original review.  Still the best I’ve found and believe will continue to be based on continual updates. 

Task management apps are like cars - some people like sports cars, some like pickups and some like high gas mileage - and some are brand loyal, so if everyone liked Chevy, Ford would be out of business. Even though todoist, things, todo, Omnifocus and many many more can do 90%-100% of what we need, how they do it, the user interface, the ease of use and ultimately,  for most I think, the enjoyment of using that particular app can run the gambit. I’ve not just tried all of the apps above, but seriously used them for quite some time; and have tried many more. This app was great when I started using it a year ago. Since then , the improvements that have been made, make it so close to perfect that I cannot come up with a single thing I’d change if I could. It is so intuitive, so clean, so simple to use, yet so feature rich. And as far as my experience, there has never been an update that wasn’t polished and perfect right out of the gate. TickTick must have a large team of VERY sharp folks working on this app. Lastly, it comes back to the enjoyment of use. The other apps I mentioned are all very good, but from features to UI, ease of input, and pure enjoyment, TickTick is in a class by itself for me. Well done TickTick, very, very well done.

title: Great app but…
body:
I’ll start by saying that (as a former Wunderlist user) I really like many things about the app. 

But customer support takes forever and sometimes no one ever responds. And if you are lucky enough to get a reply, it is scripted and has little useful information, so then you can go back and forth for days or weeks trying to resolve issues due to lag times. I’d like to see their customer support system vastly improved and beefed up, not only for those of us with paid subscriptions but also those with free accounts. An online community forum, manned by support staff, would also help. Maybe even have customer support through Twitter? A multi-pronged support system would be ideal. 

Also, the latest update for both iOS and Mac has bugs, which I’ve reported, that would probably be dealbreakers except I know that this developer updates the app a lot, so hopefully the problems will be fixed in the next update. But this could be another opportunity where a customer forum could help us understand how widespread the issues are and inform us of possible workarounds until bugs are squashed.

title: The only thing that works!
body:
I love this app. I’ve messed with bullet journals, regular planners, G**gle calenders, etc. all to varying degrees of success… but nothing has ever stuck or has been so easy to use as TickTick, mainly due to its widget function, minimal layout + pared back features, and ease of use. I wish more apps would realize that we don’t need to be able to do a million different things semi-well, as long as we can use just a few really well developed core functions, and I believe TickTick does that.
I mainly like to use its task features, not so much the habits although the feature is nice. 
There are just two things I think could make this app better, the first being for a way to set your “end of day” time in the app. By default, the new day starts at midnight, but more often than not I am still working/doing things past that time, so it’s still technically the same day for me. If I could set it to like 2am or something, it would be great and I wouldn’t have to keep postponing whatever tasks I have “leftover”. Secondly, I use the free version of the app — I wish there was a way to get the premium version with a one time payment. I understand it’s more lucrative to use a subscription model, but dang I’m just so tired of having to subscribe to apps all the time. 
Beyond that, I LOVE this app and am grateful that it’s been so helpful in my day to day life.

title: Godsend for ADHD
body:
I have struggled with severe ADHD all of my life. Even with medication, I have to work extremely hard to maintain basic “adulting” due to my executive function challenges. This app is the first thing that really keeps me on track (well, that plus a healthy dose of Vyvanse). 

General:
It’s visually clean and uncluttered, which is vital for someone with ADHD. I have my calendar, to do list, and the routine time reminders - like to take my meds and leave to go pick up my kids - in the same app rather than utilizing three different ones to get the job done. 

List:
I love that you can set a due date for every single task with reminders. This is vital! I also live that you can choose NOT to have a reminder for a take, because sometimes I need to come back to a list and just power through multiple tasks when I have time and burst of energy/focus. The tags that let you sort your tasks into categories is invaluable. Because people with ADHD have to exert more brain power to sort through a list and prioritize, it’s nice to be able to click “home cleaning” and have my list right there. (No, people with ADHD can’t just look around and see what needs to be done and do it. There’s a litany of therapists on TikTok explaining why and how to manage that. TickTick helps us do precisely what they recommend). Oh, and the fact that I can set how long a task should take is amazing! Seeing the juxtaposition of what I predicted and the actual time it took (using pomodoros, which I’ll discuss next) is a total game changer!

Pomodoro:
I can’t even begin to discuss my love of the Pomo for feature!!! Time blindness is a huge problem for people with ADHD. We tend to get lost in hyper focus and lose hours on end. The Pomo timer let’s me choose the length of my focused time and forces me to take breaks, which helps reduce the cycle of hyperfocus>mental-overexertion>>exhaustion>avoidance.  

Calendar:
Having not just my appointments, but my tasks on the calendar helps me visually plan my day so much better! Time is, again, a major area of struggle since we ADHDers don’t naturally chunk time appropriately. So seeing it all in one place, complete with estimates of how long each task will take, means I can actually plan my day for the first time in my life. 

I seriously don’t know how I survived before TickTick. Thank you for creating a truly life-changing app.

author: Marcus Bian

title: Everything I was looking for
body:
Absolutely love the app! It has everything that one needs. It’s great for managing tasks but it’s also great for habits! The habit tracker actually works. Ive tried other habit trackers but for some reason they weren’t for me. TickTick actually helped me stick to my habits for more than a month and I’m so proud of myself. I’m a pretty minimalistic person and I don’t like to have too many apps. Instead of having a calendar app, todo list app, and habit tracker app, TickTick has everything in one! The design is really nice and everything is intuitive. Ive been using TickTick for like 2 years and I felt like I should write a review because it has helped me tremendously. Whenever I have an issue, they’re quick to resolve it. I also love the achievement score feature because I can compare my “productivity” with other users. It really motivates me to do my tasks because of my competitive nature. I subscribed to premium not long ago and the calendar is so good! Different views and I like that I can put my tasks in time slots. HOWEVER, TickTick doesn’t let me to put events on the calendar as a thing that doesn’t need to be checked off that could be added and improved. The themes with premium are also very appealing. The app also has pomodoro that you can use. I have another app for that which is better imo so I don’t use the pomodoro in TickTick as often but it’s still great! 
Oh, and it has widgets and Apple Watch integration! I love that it’s on Apple Watch but one thing that could be added is the ability to check off habits on the Apple Watch as well, not just tasks. 
Overall, I’m very pleased and I don’t see myself switching to any other app anytime soon. Keep up the great work!

title: Excellent with a Few Caveats
body:
Hi, I have been using the app for a few months now and combination of habit manager and task manager in a single app is really great. I am giving 4 stars due to a few caveats I observed. I have already sent these as messages couple months ago and did not get any response. Hence I am posting here. 

1. The Today list shows the tasks and the habits. But tomorrow's list shows only the tasks. Can you please modify it to show the habits for tomorrow so I can review it the previous day and plan it accordingly.

2. We can agree that Inbox is a separate list to facilitate the GTD methodology. The tasks are still in the inbox even after I assign them to a particular date. The task is removed from Inbox only when I add it to any list. I have a few tasks that do not go on any list but just need to be reminded on that day. I don't want them in my inbox after I reviewed it and assigned a date. 
At least implement a filter in the inbox to show tasks without any due date. 

3. Skipping a habit is not syncing to other devices. I don’t think it’s a sync issue as marking it as achieved or unachieved is being reflected in other devices. So essentially even if I skip a habit in my iPhone , it is still showing up in Today on my Mac. Please sync the skipping action to other devices. 

Thank you

title: An Honest Perspective
body:
This application is very well suited for people to organize their lives in one place. Physical planners tend to have monthly calendars, weekly calendars, daily to-do lists and even some form of habit tracking and this is the only application that offers that in a friendly interface. 

Room for improvement would be to add a “project functionality,” but that can be achieved a number of ways with the current software without the written designation. It could also use a deadline function similar to Things3 and a “plan ahead” function that takes the events yet to be assigned a deadline or due date then helps you organize them into your schedule according to the time it takes to complete the task and the openings you have within a given period of time (which would be scalable for people looking to achieve long term or short term goals/projects)

A personal note—I was hit by a car recently and have a degree of memory problems and this application is a life saver for me. Having habits, calendars and my to-do list all in one place helps me immensely. I always know ai need to check in with one app and not three. The collaboration elements help me coordinate with others during COVID as well.

title: The app is mentally challenged. It tracks tasks fine though

The place where this app really flops is the smart input. In practice, I write “blah blah Wednesday 22:00” and the app highlights “wed” and “22:00” and schedules it for TUESDAY AT 22:00, leaving me with a list item called “blah blah nesday”
I write “blah blah wed 22:00” and it schedules it for TUESDAY at 22:00. It’s mentally challenged.
author: + DonSmilo +

title: Would have been perfect except...
body:
TickTick was ALMOST exactly what I’d been looking for forever. It had most of the task features of Things, plus some extra cool ones that Things doesn’t have. I loved the theme options that make it so attractive to look at. The biggest thing it has on all the other apps like it is the built-in calendar feature, so you don’t have to use a separate app for scheduling. You can manage your whole life from one app! I thought it was my dream come true! I’ve tried almost every productivity app there is, and this was the only one that seemed to have everything I was looking for. 

But it turned out there is ONE fatal flaw I just can’t live with. I tried to at first, but I just couldn’t. It’s the recurring tasks. As soon as you complete one, the new task appears immediately to replace it instead of being delayed and appearing the next day/week/etc., like with most apps. It will just have faint text next to it indicating that it’s for a later date, but the task is still in your list, so it’s impossible to forget about it and get it out of your mind until it’s time to do it. It just clutters up your task list with a task it’s not even time to do yet (or in my case, up to 10 tasks!) 

So if you have a list of 10 tasks for the day, all of them daily recurring tasks, every time you complete one, another duplicate task immediately appears to replace it, so your list will continue to have 10 items on it no matter how many you complete, and it’s difficult to tell at a glance which items you’ve completed and which ones you haven’t. The only way you can tell is to look at the faint text next to a task that tells you it’s for tomorrow, but that’s kind of tedious. You can’t tell at a glance. 

The whole point of checking items off a to-do list is so you can easily see which ones you’ve completed, plus you get the satisfaction of seeing your list get smaller the more things you do. If you have a list of recurring tasks, you don’t get that benefit, which kind of defeats the purpose of having a to do list. 

For such a robust and well-thought-out app, I’m surprised that this one little feature was so poorly planned out. I really hope that maybe one day they’ll consider changing it, because in that case, I’d love to give TickTick another try.

I’ve noticed that I can sort my task mode lists by the date the task is due (so that tasks due earliest are on top of list) but not in note mode. Regarding time/date, I am only able to sort by created time or modified time, which doesn’t apply to due date.

title: Almost perfect
body:
I usually don’t write review but I really wanted to share my TickTick experience.

I’ve been looking for years for an app that can deal with both Calendar events and Tasks management. Tick Tick seems te be the good deal. I love the idea to be able to add checklists in my events timeline. For example, I can add “Groceries shopping” on my timeline as a task, choose how long it should take to complete and then add a checklist of the items I need to purchase in the task. Or when I want to batch things to do, I add a task on my timeline that says “To Do” and then I add the checklist of all the things I have to do.

If you’re like me and like to visualize your tasks AND events on one timeline, TickTick is the real deal.

However there are a few things that could be done to make it better and a few glitches that should be fixed:

- The possibility to see your Calendar events along with your tasks on your Apple Watch. Right now on the watch you can only see your tasks.

- You guys at TickTick should add the possibility to create Calendars in your app not in third party apps or local calendars. There are a few annoying glitches when trying to modify iCal events in TickTick which is annoying since it’s forcing me to use my iCal in a second window.

- Also there is no way to modify a single occurence of a recurring task. For example, I have tasks that I accomplish daily, usually at the same time everyday but some days, my schedule changes and I cannot change the time of only one occurence of that task. This is why I’m taking off a star because this is a function that is essential in a calendar / task management app.

- An Alexa integration would be an amazing addition to make this app the perfect assistant.

- A widget that would show both your Calendar events and tasks would be a plus too.

Now, i have all the tools I need in the app to time block with ease, and I subscribe to the TickTick calendar feed to see my task schedule in whatever calendar I want, mostly in my corporate Exchange calendars in Outlook.  I think ToDoist still does some things better Than TickTick, but those things are insignificant compared to TickTick’s time blocking capabilities.  4 stars so far because some of the navigation around the app is difficult, and because I can’t login to the Windows app with my Apple ID (support request pending). title: Expected More
body: There seemed to be some hype around this product, and I kind of expected more. I’ll just write why I didn’t have a good experience and decided not to bother. First, I decided to import from my Reminders app, and the first thing it ask was if I wanted to “Import and Delete” or just “Import”. Please get rid of the “Import and Delete” option, as it’s very deadly. Reason is because, after deciding I wanted to sync with another device I created an account. First thing that popped up after that, was that I had too many lists, and asked me to upgrade. I declined, to see how many lists I went over (and so you know, I think it’s 10, but I can’t see anywhere that mentions how many you get on the free tier). So after declining, what did I see - nothing. Yup, nothing, everything was gone. All my lists, to dos, etc, all gone. Even the free stuff they put in there was all gone. You know what, I was lucky not to click “Import and Delete” so all my stuff was still in my Reminders app. Imagine how many people went through this, and decided to delete their stuff before knowing it works! So, after that I decided to give it another try and import yet again. This time, I saw indicators on lists that did not sync because I was over my limit. Fine, so I spent some time managing my to-dos and reduced down to like 8 lists. I don’t have a lot of things, but I liked to keep things separate. At any rate, after what seemed like things synced up, I logged in on my iPad, and there is this one stubborn list that just did not want to sync! No matter what I tried, it did not sync. So I created a new list on my phone (list showed up on my iPad) and then I moved all my items over from the missing list to the new list. I expected all my items to show up in my iPad as well. Guess what, they didn’t. I also had stuff in another Inbox list on my iPad that was not appearing on my phone. Web was the same as iPad. So, I don’t know what’s going on, but it did not sit well with me. I’m not going to bother buying into this if it didn’t even work well first time around. I expected it to work, plain and simple. 3 stars for what could have been a nice product, but I’m not going to risk losing my stuff again.

I’ve tried a ridiculous number of “To Do” apps over the years and nothing has been great for my needs. 
I need folder and task priority organizing options, simplicity, and cross-platform capability. This app does all that for me. It’s on my work PC, cell phone, iPad, and MacBook. That is extremely important for me because if I can’t keep these lists on my personal and work devices, their utility goes way down.
The first daily habit I added was to check TickTick and my calendars. That was a good move. 
I hope in 6 months I’m still using this app because right now it’s 5 stars for me.

title: Best Productivity/Notes App Ever
body:
I have tried a lot of apps to help manage tasks, track habits, and stay focused but none have measured up to TickTick. The app/website is clean and simple so you don’t get overwhelmed with the things you want to accomplish - which is what I want in an app. 

But the reason I love the app is the features. It is everything I was looking for bundled in one and provided a better user experience an the competition, too. 

1. Habit Tracker - easy and fun to use
2. Tasks/Notes - nothing too crazy or out of the box here - but effective 
3. Focus timer/stopwatch - this is my favorite feature. It’s SO well integrated in the apps it makes a breeze to actually use on a daily bases. 

Then, the thing that make it all possible to use in today’s society is the apps. The app for Mac is awesome. When the app is enabled there’s a small emblem telling you how many tasks you have or how much time is left on to focus depending a quick to configure toggle.

Lastly, it can sync to you calendar which can be a big deal if you manage your life off your calendar. 

My suggestion to TickTick, I would like to see is more options when it comes to alerts on tasks and option for the sound that notifies you when your focus timer has ended. 

My suggestion to you (the person try to better manager to time and habits)... Download it!!

Overall, a well deserved 5-Star rating!! Good work, keep it up.

title: LOVE the app, but...
body:
So let me just start off by saying this app has kept me so organized ever since I downloaded it and it is very convenient. The tags and lists are a great feature that I definitely am using, the personalization for each task is great, and the calendar is extremely easy to use. However, there is one problem. When I say one problem, I mean out of the whole app I have found only one problem (which is fantastic!). The problem is that when I’m not able to get something done that I put in as a task for the day, there is no option for incomplete. The only options are to mark it as complete (which effects the statistics) or leave it alone and it runs into the next day as overdue; but, I don’t want a lot of the tasks I can’t get done in the overdue section. The other button it has is a delete button, but then I can’t go back and see the task as incomplete because it’s gone. If I choose delete task and it’s something I have set to repeat (like my workouts), it automatically deletes all of the future workout tasks. What I’m trying to say is that I really need an incomplete or something like that button. 

I hope you see this feedback and can get back to me about fixing the problem. Thanks for the otherwise perfect app!
